summary: Quests, quizzes, quest dialogue, quest indicators and the quest log (repo root C:\Users\itech\.t3\worktrees\maplestory-isometric\t3code-d299c8ce). The quest data is correct. All 20 records in game/data/canonical/quests/1000-1019.json match the cached MeowDB quest pages on every gameplay field: exp, mesos, levelMin, jobReq, requiresAll, need (mobs and items), get, acceptItems and rewardRandom were compared with a node script over tools/meowdb/.cache/quest-tracker_10xx.html. The live capture tools/meowdb/captures/quest_tracker_maple_island.txt confirms the same 20-quest set: 5 chains and 4 standalone quests. The live page also tags every quest "Missable" (and "COT2"), and neither the cache nor our records have that field. The generic engine is data-driven and complete in design: availability, accept items, next_quest_grants dedup, kill, use and talk objectives, hand-ins, EXP, mesos, items and lost-item re-issue. Random rewards are not first-option: one item is drawn per group, weighted by chance_pct with the injected RNG (quest_def.gd:138-140, quest_engine.gd:656-667), with seeded tests (test_quest_engine.gd:315-358) and one in-game draw for 1008. Rain's 7 quizzes are real menus graded against canonical correct_choice_index. Each wrong answer shows its paired canonical wrong-answer line, the quest stays in progress and talking again retries. 1018's answer is inferred. Quizzes are not auto-completed, except by the debug command 'quest_complete force'. Quest indicators exist with three states (QuestMarker: gold !, grey ..., green ?) and were checked in the real game on 5 NPCs. The Quest Log shows name, status, start and turn-in NPC, journal, objective quantities and rewards. It shows no chain step, quest group, map or missable tag. QuestLog persists all progress, but the random reward actually received is not recorded, and quest_progressed does not request an autosave. Main gaps: (1) only 1002, 1006, 1007 and 1008 were played in the real game; the other 16 are unit-tested or untested (1004 and 1005 have no quest-specific test; quizzes 1014-1017 are never graded in any test). (2) Quest-gated drops are missing entirely: DropRoller has no quest input, and drop_rates.json:141 says Board and Screw drop at any time. (3) BLOCKER from another domain: 1012 cannot be completed in the real game because no Wooden Box runtime exists. (4) The Quest Log lacks chain progress, and the persistence of received random rewards is missing.

defects.title: Pio's quest 1012 cannot be completed in the real game
defects.detail: Its only item sources, Rusty Screw 441 and Old Wooden Board 442, drop from the Wooden Box (breakable 0000001, 19 placements). No breakable actor or system exists in game/scripts/actors or game/scripts/world; DropRoller only mentions it in comments. DEFERRED.md:16-17 confirms the runtime is not built. The engine path is unit-tested (test_quest_engine.gd:373-389), but the DoD requires every quest played. This depends on the breakables domain.

defects.title: Quest-gated drops are not implemented
defects.detail: DropRoller.roll(owner_id, db, rng) (drop_roller.gd:21-24) has no quest or character context, and DropRates entries have no gate field. drop_rates.json:138-147 gives 441/442 a placeholder chance of 0.5 and says 'they drop at any time'. That contradicts the source decision: KuroDB reactor 2001 'Chance value 1 | Quest 1008' (MeowDB 1012) means 100% and only while 1012 is active. KuroDB also gates the Jr. Sentinel Shellpiece ('100.00% base | Quest 1035', tools/kurodb/captures/9300018.json); there is no crosswalk for that quest id.

defects.title: 16 of 20 quests have never been played in the real game
defects.detail: Real-game coverage: test_e_quest (1002, 1006, 1007, 1008) and test_d_inventory (1006). Never played: 1000, 1001, 1003, 1004, 1005, 1009, 1010, 1011, 1012 and the whole Rain quiz chain 1013-1019. The brief's 'Full Quest Playthrough Requirement' and DoD 'Every quest has been tested through actual gameplay' are unmet. DEFERRED.md:14-15 says the same.

defects.title: Quest Log has no chain progression, location or missable information
defects.detail: QuestDef.from_records (quest_def.gd:76-173) never reads quest_line, quest_group or any missable field; a grep for quest_line|quest_group|missable in game/scripts returns nothing. quest_window.gd shows 'From X, turn in to Y' but no chain step (e.g. Mai's Training 2/3, Rain's Maple Quiz 4/7), no map name for NPCs and no received random reward. The brief asks for 'chain progression where useful' and a quest UI that 'supports the complete Maple Island quest set'.

defects.title: The random reward actually received is not persisted
defects.detail: complete() returns random_picks (quest_engine.gd:456), but QuestLog entries (quest_log.gd:6-20) store no reward record, so only the item in the inventory remembers it. Brief Phase 14 lists 'random quest rewards already received' and the DoD lists 'random reward state persists'. This needs QuestLog format 2 with a migration from format 1.

defects.title: quest_progressed does not request an autosave
defects.detail: AUTOSAVE_TRIGGERS (game_state.gd:54-55) are map_entered, leveled_up, quest_started, quest_completed and quest_forfeited. Kill and use progress is saved only at the next milestone, a manual save or quit-save, so a crash loses it. The autosave is debounced (2 s / 15 s max), so adding the trigger is cheap.

defects.title: Live MeowDB 'Missable' flag (and 'COT2' tag) not recorded
defects.detail: The capture tools/meowdb/captures/quest_tracker_maple_island.txt (2026-10-05) shows 'COT2 · Missable' on all 20 quests. The cached payload has no such key (grep for 'missable' over the quest-tracker caches returns 0), so the records lack it. When a dated live capture differs from the cache, the capture is newer, so it should be added with capture provenance. Do not interpret 'COT2'.

defects.title: Quizzes 1014-1017 never graded in any test; 1004/1005 have no quest-specific test
defects.detail: 1014-1017 appear only as force-completed prerequisites (test_quest_engine.gd:454-456; test_dialogue_npc_conversations.gd:390-392). 1019's wrong answers are untested. 1004 and 1005 are referenced by no test beyond generic offer and validation sweeps. Wrong-line pairing was checked by hand for all 7 quizzes and is correct, but nothing pins it.

defects.title: Headless DataValidator skips quest/NPC/dialogue validation
defects.detail: QuestCatalog.validate, NpcCatalog.validate and NpcDialogueBuilder.validate_all run only inside unit tests. data_validator.gd and tools/validate_data.gd never call them (docs/runtime/QUESTS_AND_DIALOGUE.md:312-315 calls this a known gap).

defects.title: No player-facing forfeit; the documented 1002 workaround needs the console
defects.detail: Forfeit exists only in QuestEngine/QuestService and the debug 'quest forfeit' command. The quest window states it 'never changes quest state'. docs/runtime/QUESTS_AND_DIALOGUE.md:320-321 says a lost Roger's Apple can be fixed by forfeiting and re-accepting, which the brief's 'no developer console' rule rules out.

defects.title: Yes/No prompt is the last On-accept line even when it is a statement
defects.detail: npc_dialogue_builder.gd:147-156 turns the last On-accept line into the yes_no node. For 1000 that line is the Quest Helper tip (A3), and for 1014-1019 it is 'talk to me when you're ready for the next question'. MeowDB does not mark which line is the prompt, so this is an adaptation. It is not listed in the adaptations table or in the parity rows.

defects.title: Turn-in objective says 'Return to X' when X was never met
defects.detail: ui_text.gd:57-59 renders every npc_talk turn_in row as 'Return to <end NPC>', e.g. 'Return to Mai' for 1006 and 'Return to Sera' for 1000. It is only accurate when the start and end NPC are the same.

open_questions: Does KuroDB 'Quest 1035' on the Tutorial Jr. Sentinel's Jr. Sentinel Shellpiece correspond to MeowDB 1005 (Todd's How-to-Hunt)? If so, should the Shellpiece also be quest-gated? No quest-id crosswalk exists in the repo; the reactor capture infers only Kuro 1008 = MeowDB 1012.
What does a quest gate mean exactly: drop only while the quest is in progress, or also stop once the required count is held? KuroDB only says 'Quest N'. The minimal sourced rule is 'in progress'.

Yes/No prompt fidelity: for 1000 (last On-accept line is the Quest Helper tip) and 1014-1019 (a single statement line), should the statement stay as the prompt, or should those lines become say pages followed by the generic system offer_prompt? MeowDB does not mark the prompt line. This needs a project-owner decision because both choices are adaptations.
Should Rain's next quiz be offered in the same conversation after a correct answer? The current flow ends the chat after the right answer, and the next quiz needs a new talk. MeowDB is silent.
'Missable' applies to all 20 quests, but departure from Maple Island (Shanks) is out of scope. Should MisoStory warn at Shanks about unfinished missable quests, or only record the flag for now?
Roger's Apple at full HP heals nothing (test_e: HP 50 -> 50). MeowDB records no quest-start HP change (docs/canonical/quests.md §8). Should this stay as-is (no unsourced effect)?

Should a player-facing give-up exist at all? If not, the documented 1002 lost-apple workaround in docs/runtime/QUESTS_AND_DIALOGUE.md:320-321 must be removed or replaced (e.g. a MisoStory re-issue adaptation).

summary: The canonical data for NPCs and shops is complete and matches the MeowDB cache exactly. I re-ran tools/meowdb/extract_npcs.mjs and extract_shops.mjs on a temp copy of tools/meowdb/.cache: network_fetches 0, and the output is byte-identical to game/data/canonical/npcs (21 files) and game/data/canonical/shops (3 files). Three independent cache views give the same scope. The /npcs index has region MapleIsland for exactly ids 1-21. The /npc-shops index lists 43 shops, and town maple-road holds only maple-road-pan (16), maple-road-sid (20) and maple-road-lucy (21). The "Where to buy" rows of all 95 canonical items name only Pan (13 ids), Sid (4) and Lucy (6) as Maple Island sellers. MeowDB lists no other Maple Island shop or shop NPC. Paul, Tia and the Maple Administrator are correctly absent: no MeowDB Maple Island record, no Blender marker, and test_map_definitions requires the runtime NPCs to be exactly MeowDB's. In the runtime, all 21 NPCs are placed from Blender markers matched by meowdb_npc_id, and all 21 were talked to on foot in the real game (baseline npcs scenario 66/66, talk_gap -0.61 to -1.67 m). Quest and shop associations are cross-validated against the quest records (NpcCatalog.validate). All three shops work against canonical stock, order, prices and sell-back (test_g_shop 184/184, plus test_shop_buy_sell and test_shop_ui_window): quantity, insufficient mesos, full Equip/Use tabs and stacking are all covered. No Maple Island row is rechargeable, so recharging does not apply. Open problems: (1) Shanks (npc 15) has his canonical transport (Lith Harbor, 300 mesos, level 7) disabled by misostory/npcs/15.json, and the only thing he does is say idle line 0. The Iteration Three "Southperry departure boundary" does not exist yet. (2) ShopService.quote_sell lets the player sell untradeable quest items. Selling Roger's Apple (235) while quest 1002 is in progress makes 1002 impossible to complete: there is no lost-item re-issue branch and no player-facing forfeit. (3) Idle chatter, which MeowDB describes as the speech-bubble pool, never reaches the player outside shop greetings and Shanks. (4) The rule that picks dialogue line 0 or the last line by quest state, and the "<NPC>'s Shop" title, are MisoStory inferences that live in code with no adaptation record. (5) No console-free, clean-character run uses any shop: test_g_shop relies on warp and mesos console setup, and test_c_progression never visits a shop.

defects.title: Shanks' departure (the Iteration Three boundary) is not implemented
defects.detail: game/data/misostory/npcs/15.json sets disabled_behaviors ['transport']. Its reason still says 'out of scope for Iteration Two'. NpcDialogueBuilder has no code for the transport behaviour at all, so re-enabling the flag would do nothing. Talking to Shanks only shows idle_chatter[0], 'I'm the captain, dang it! Don't look down on me!' (test_dialogue_npc_conversations.test_shanks_only_talks). Canonical record npcs/15.json transport: 000000060 -> 010000000 Lith Harbor, fare 300, min_level 7, one_way, from the cached beginner guide, which also says 'Hand in every Maple Island quest before you board.' The brief requires 'arrive at Southperry ready to leave Maple Island' and 'The Southperry departure boundary is enough.' Right now nothing in the game marks or checks that boundary.

defects.title: Selling Roger's Apple during quest 1002 makes the quest permanently uncompletable
defects.detail: ShopService.quote_sell (game/scripts/core/shop/shop_service.gd:114-137) checks neither ItemDef.tradeable nor quest_item, and inventory.json shop.sell_zero_value_items=true, so the shop accepts the item for 0 mesos. Quest 1002's only objective is item_usage of 235 x1. The apple is handed out on accept by misostory/quests/1002.json. The quest's only completion branch is stopItem, with no lost/re-issue. There is no player-facing forfeit (forfeit exists only in debug_commands.gd). Scenario: accept 1002, walk to Lucy, Pan or Sid without eating the apple, sell it, and 1002 can never be completed without the console. That contradicts the DoD item 'complete every Maple Island quest'. The same unguarded path also sells 347, 438, 439, 440, 441, 442, 483 and 522 The Green Relaxer (the unique, untradeable chair rewarded by 1012). 1001, 1007 and 1008 recover through their lost branches, and 441, 442 and 347 can be farmed again, but the chair and the apple cannot be recovered.

defects.title: No console-free, clean-character use of any shop
defects.detail: The DoD Gameplay section requires 'use every Maple Island shop' and 'no developer console'. test_c_progression.gd has no shop step. test_g_shop reaches Pan and Sid with 'warp' and funds every purchase with 'mesos' console commands (baseline report steps 1, 11, 33, 52, 56). The shop mechanics themselves are verified. Real use with earned mesos is not.

defects.title: Canonical idle chatter (speech bubbles) never reaches the player
defects.detail: Every NPC has a canonical idle_chatter pool: Heena 8, Sera 9, Roger 9, Peter, Todd, Robin and Sam 10 each, and so on. Many lines are tutorial hints (Todd: 'Press Ctrl to attack monsters.', 'Press Z to pick up items.'). NpcDef.idle_line (npc_def.gd:90) has no runtime caller. Players see idle lines only as the shop greetings of 16, 20 and 21 and as Shanks' talk line.

defects.title: The rule that picks the first or last 'What X Says' line is a code-only adaptation
defects.detail: npc_dialogue_builder.gd:297-311 shows dialogue[0] until all of the NPC's quests are completed, then the last line. MeowDB does not label the lines (docs/canonical/npcs.md, Gaps). No adaptation record has a reason or verified flag, so the Phase 17 provenance audit cannot see it. Some lines are shown at the wrong moment: Sera's 'Did you give my mirror to Heena?' and Sen's 'What did my sister say?' read as in-progress lines but appear after completion.

defects.title: Gaps in test_g_shop coverage
defects.detail: Not exercised in the real game: selling an Etc monster drop (e.g. Snail Shell 348, sell 1; Blue Snail Shell 349, sell 2; Orange Mushroom Cap 356, sell 8), which is the island's real meso source; selling Apple and Orange; selling an equipment instance with rolled stats through the window (only unit tested: test_shop_buy_sell.test_sell_slot_sells_that_instance); any attempt to sell a quest item; buying 9 of Pan's 13 rows (they are displayed and price-checked only).

defects.title: Stale and uncited text in the NPC/shop adaptations
defects.detail: misostory/npcs/15.json's reason refers to Iteration Two scope. The shop window title '%s's Shop' (shop_window.gd:117) is MisoStory wording that no adaptation record names (MeowDB has no shop title). test_map_definitions.gd:195 still allows 'Mai' as an extra Blender marker, although Mai's marker is now matched.

implementation_plan.step: 2. Make NPC/shop canonical parity re-provable
implementation_plan.detail: Add a --verify mode to tools/meowdb/extract_npcs.mjs and extract_shops.mjs. It extracts into a temp dir from the cache only, diffs against game/data/canonical/{npcs,shops} and exits non-zero on any difference. Call it from scripts/validate_data.sh when tools/meowdb/.cache exists, and skip with a note when the cache is absent, since the cache is git-ignored.
implementation_plan.tests: Run validate_data.sh with the cache present: no differences.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Implement the Southperry departure boundary at Shanks
implementation_plan.detail: Generic, data-driven, built on existing systems. (a) NpcDialogueBuilder gets _add_transport(g, n), generated from n.transport.routes (nothing NPC-specific in code). The talk node branches on condition {level:{min:min_level}} and {mesos:{min:fare_mesos}}. A failing condition shows a MisoStory system line. Otherwise a yes_no offer (system text, since MeowDB has no boarding text) leads to a new DialogueContext action 'depart' {route}. That action re-checks the conditions, applies the fare per the owner's decision, and emits an effect {type:'departure_requested', to_map_id, fare}. (b) NpcInteraction re-emits it as a signal, as it already does for shop_requested, and the game shell shows an explicit end-of-Maple-Island notice. Victoria Island is not built, so the map does not change. Optionally a character flag records 'reached_departure'. (c) Add system lines transport_offer, transport_level_too_low, transport_not_enough_mesos, departure_boundary and open_quests_warning to misostory/dialogue/_system.json, each with reason and verified:false. The open-quests warning quotes the guide's advice to hand in every quest before boarding. (d) Rewrite misostory/npcs/15.json: remove disabled 'transport' and give an Iteration Three reason.
implementation_plan.tests: Replace test_npc_catalog.test_shanks_transport_disabled_by_adaptation with a check that transport is enabled from the canonical route. Replace test_dialogue_npc_conversations.test_shanks_only_talks with three cases: level 6 is refused; level 7 with 299 mesos is refused; level 7 with 300 mesos reaches the boundary (mesos change per the decision). Data validation must accept the new system keys. The clean-character playthrough ends by talking to Shanks.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Guard against selling quest-critical items
implementation_plan.detail: In ShopService.quote_sell, refuse an item that an in-progress quest still needs and that cannot be re-issued. The source list is canonical items_given_on_accept plus misostory quests/*.json accept_items, filtered to quests without a lost_items branch. Add a QuestEngine helper and a new ItemCodes.QUEST_ITEM_IN_USE with a message. Put the rule in inventory.json shop.block_selling_open_quest_items {value, reason: 'MeowDB documents no sell restriction; avoids a 1002 softlock', verified:false}. Alternative, if the owner prefers it: give Roger a re-issue for 1002 through a quest adaptation (his canonical stopItem line, 'Eat the Roger's Apple I gave you', fits) and leave selling open. Whether to protect The Green Relaxer (522) is an owner decision.
implementation_plan.tests: test_shop_buy_sell: Roger's Apple sale refused while 1002 is in progress and allowed after; Sera's Mirror during 1001 follows the rule chosen. test_shop_ui_window: the refusal message is shown. test_g_shop: try to sell Roger's Apple mid-1002 in the real game.

implementation_plan.step: 5. Extend the shop playtests and add shops to the clean playthrough
implementation_plan.detail: test_g_shop: sell an Etc drop (Snail Shell 348, Blue Snail Shell 349 or Orange Mushroom Cap 356) at its canonical per-unit sell-back; sell Apple and Orange; sell a dropped equipment instance with rolled stats through the window; buy the 9 Pan rows not yet bought (one each); try a quest-item sale (step 4). Phase 15 clean-character scenario (with or after test_c_progression): no console. Buy potions from Lucy with mesos earned from drops, buy a weapon from Sid, buy at least one Pan item, and sell drops. Check the meso ledger against canonical prices.
implementation_plan.tests: Both scenarios PASS. The report shows 0 console steps for the clean run.

implementation_plan.step: 6. NPC speech bubbles from canonical idle chatter
implementation_plan.detail: Add a screen-space bubble to NpcPresenter (new game/scripts/actors/npcs/npc_speech_bubble.gd). It shows NpcDef.idle_line(i) for current-map, on-screen NPCs and is suppressed while that NPC is in dialogue. Interval, display time and order go in presentation.json npc.speech_bubbles {interval_s, display_s, order, reason, verified:false}, because MeowDB gives no timing.
implementation_plan.tests: Unit test: every bubble text equals a canonical idle_chatter line, with a seeded order. npcs scenario: a bubble is observed for at least one NPC per map and its text is canonical.

implementation_plan.step: 7. Record the default-talk rule and UI wording as adaptations
implementation_plan.detail: Move the d0/d1 rule from npc_dialogue_builder.gd:297-311 into data, e.g. misostory/dialogue/_talk_rules.json {rule:'first_until_all_own_quests_completed_then_last', reason, verified:false}, with optional per-NPC overrides. Owner decides whether Sera and Sen should show d1 while their quest is in progress. Document '<npc>'s Shop' (shop_window.gd:117) as MisoStory UI text, or build the title from canonical fields (name plus function_title).
implementation_plan.tests: test_dialogue_npc_conversations: for each quest NPC, the before and after lines match the rule file. Data validation: the rule file has reason and verified.

Label shopkeepers with function_title. Spawn placement: 'avoid NPC interaction spaces' should use WorldTuning.talk_zone radii (1.6 m default, 2.4 m across_counter). Quest markers already exist.

summary:
I checked all 95 local canonical items (game/data/canonical/items/*.json) against the cached MeowDB item API (tools/meowdb/.cache/api_items_<id>_q_locale_en_preview_1.html). Fields compared: name, type, subtype, game id/iconKey, level, job, the STR/DEX/INT/LUK/fame requirements, every stat row, attack speed, consumable HP/MP, chair bonus, sell price, stack size and scroll success. There are no real mismatches. The only differences are expected representation choices: scroll bonuses live in scroll.stat_bonus_on_success, and max_stack comes from the item page's "Max per Stack" row because the API omits slotMax. Pet Food's npc_buy_price_mesos of 30 is the cheapest price anywhere, which is documented; Lucy's row correctly charges 35. ShopService uses each shop's own price, so this is not a defect.

The runtime item core is complete and well tested: ItemDef, the 5-tab Inventory (Setup included), Equipment (requirements, slots, overall and two-handed conflicts), Consumables (flat or percent HP/MP), ItemService and ShopService. The Setup tab exists and stores chairs: Inventory.TABS, "Set-up" in the inventory, shop and tooltip windows, save to_dict/from_dict, and test_inventory_core.gd uses 522.

**The Green Relaxer (522) can NOT be used as a chair.** There is no sitting system. ItemDef only reads setup_hp_bonus and setup_interval_s for the tooltip. inventory_window.activate_slot returns NOT_USABLE for Setup items. test_consumable_use.gd:97 asserts 522 is not usable. The "sit" key (X) is reserved but listed in controls_panel.gd NOT_AVAILABLE. natural_recovery.gd has no seated state. This fails the Definition of Done: "chairs work", "obtain and use a chair", and Pio's reward.

**No other chair belongs to Maple Island.** 525 Sky-blue Wooden Chair is local, but it is sold by Mina in Lith Harbor (Victoria Island). No Hidden Street drop list has a Setup item. MeowDB's map data documents no benches, even though Rain's quiz dialogue mentions "chairs or benches".

**Item closure for Iteration Three.** The needed set is 55 local items plus 29 Hidden Street drop members with no local definition. The local 55 are: 3 creation weapons, 21 quest items (including the random hats 708-715 and Razor/Fruit Knife), 23 shop rows, the 4 Wooden Box items, and 22 Hidden Street drop members.
- **Green Apple (MeowDB 242) is the only one of the 29 that would actually drop at runtime.** KuroDB gives it 2% on Snail, Blue Snail, Shroom and Red Snail. Its capture (tools/meowdb/captures/items_api.json) is API-only, with no "Max per Stack" row. Imported as-is, ItemDef would fall back to unpublished_max_stack = 1. Green Apple also restores 30 MP, not HP.
- **Omok Piece: Mushroom has a KuroDB chance (1%) but stays unresolved.** It is ambiguous between 486, 495 and 498 (decision D3-8).
- **The other 27 have no KuroDB chance, so they never drop.** They only need resolving to an id so validation can show them.
  - 23 of them have a MeowDB id found in the cache (mostly from /npc-shops rows) but no cached item page.
  - Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword and Pistol have no MeowDB id anywhere in the 1050 cached files.
  - Blue Cloth Vest (M) could be 949 or 958, and Black Cloth Pants (F) is 1179 by list position only; both need a gender check.

**40 local items fall out of the closure** (old MeowDB-community drop entries: ores, scrolls, higher-level gear, 525). Saves, formulas/recovery.json and combat tests still reference them, so they should be kept.

**Placeholder or unverified gameplay values in item handling (game/data/misostory/):**
- drop_rates.json is the only file of kind misostory_placeholder: every drop chance, quantity and meso amount in it is a placeholder. Owner: drops domain.
- combat.json natural_recovery resets the timer instead of pausing it, adds a 5 s combat delay, and has no seated state. Owner: mechanics domain.
- inventory.json (24 slots per tab, meso cap, slot conflicts, two-handed flags, pirate job tags), drops.json (ground lifetime and ownership) and new_character.json (empty starting inventory) are labelled, unverified adaptations.

**Extraction cannot be reproduced for new items.**
- The lib.mjs header says the extractors re-run from the captures, but fetchUrl only reads the git-ignored .cache.
- extract_items.mjs uses a hardcoded ITEM_IDS list and deletes any item file not on it.

I made no file changes.

defects.title: The Green Relaxer (522) is not usable as a chair; no sitting system exists
defects.detail: Pio's quest 1012 gives 522 (test_quest_engine.gd:386), and it lands in the Setup tab. Nothing can be done with it after that. ItemDef reads setup_hp_bonus and setup_interval_s only for the tooltip (item_def.gd:165-167, item_tooltip.gd:197-198). inventory_window.activate_slot returns NOT_USABLE for anything that is neither equipment nor a consumable (inventory_window.gd:170-178). test_consumable_use.gd:97 asserts 522 is not usable. Controls bind 'sit' to X (controls.gd:20), but controls_panel.gd:16 lists it as NOT_AVAILABLE. player_controller.gd:47 has no seated state. This fails the Definition of Done: 'chairs work', 'obtain and use a chair', 'Sitting permits natural HP regeneration', and Phase 9.

defects.title: Green Apple (MeowDB 242) is a runtime drop with a KuroDB chance but has no local definition
defects.detail: Hidden Street lists Green Apple for Snail, Blue Snail, Shroom and Red Snail. KuroDB gives it 2.00% base on all four (100100, 100101, 120100, 130101), so after the drop pass it will roll. There is no game/data/canonical/items/242.json. The only capture, tools/meowdb/captures/items_api.json, is the API body: Use/Food, mpRecover 30, price 3, iconKey 2010007. The API has no slotMax, so a file built from it alone gets max_stack null, and ItemDef falls back to unpublished_max_stack = 1 (inventory.json), meaning one apple per Use slot. The item-db/242 page ('Max per Stack' row, Untradeable tag) must be read by hand. Green Apple restores 30 MP, not HP, so it must not be modelled on Apple (236).

defects.title: 28 more Hidden Street drop members have no local item definition and no cached MeowDB item page
defects.detail: These never roll, because none has a KuroDB chance, apart from Omok Piece (1%), which is unresolved. They still have to resolve so validation and the parity manifest can show them. 23 have a MeowDB id from the cache, mostly from /npc-shops table rows: 944, 916, 625, 727, 721, 720, 650, 949 (or 958), 722, 1319, 717, 1435, 943, 951, 735, 617, 1318, 1170, 718, 672, 956, 1169, 1179. Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword and Pistol have no MeowDB id anywhere in the 1050 cached files. Omok Piece: Mushroom is ambiguous between 486, 495 and 498 (D3-8). None has an item-db_<id>.html or api_items_<id> page in the cache, so each needs a manual browser read.

defects.title: Extractor cannot reproduce new items from tracked captures; the comment claims it can
defects.detail: tools/meowdb/lib.mjs lines 3-5 say the extractors re-run from .cache AND from tools/meowdb/captures/. fetchUrl (lines 59-74) reads only the git-ignored .cache and otherwise throws 'not cached'. extract_items.mjs:40-46 hardcodes ITEM_IDS (plus shop and starter-weapon ids), and line 998 deletes any items/*.json not in that list. Adding the 29 items reproducibly needs two things: a capture fallback using the same cacheKey, and an id list derived from the quests, breakable, crosswalk and drop tables. The deletion must not remove the 40 out-of-closure items, which saves, formulas/recovery.json and combat tests still reference.

defects.title: Data shape for unresolved drop members conflicts with test_drops_data.gd
defects.detail: The 'UNRESOLVED stays visible' rule means drop tables will hold Hidden Street names with no MeowDB id (Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword, Pistol, Omok Piece). reference_checks.gd accepts null for typed keys. test_drops_data.gd:11-12 asserts db().has('items', String(e.item_id)) for every entry, and DropRates.effective_entries iterates the same entries. An entry with item_id null therefore fails the suite. Unresolved members need either a separate list with a non-typed key (e.g. hidden_street_name) or an explicit chance_status that the test and DropRates skip. Owner: drops domain; this is a constraint from the items side.

defects.title: drop_rates.json placeholder chances/quantities/mesos still drive item drops (owner: drops domain)
defects.detail: game/data/misostory/drop_rates.json is kind misostory_placeholder. Equip 0.005, Etc/Monster Drop 0.4, Use/Potion 0.02, Use/Scroll 0.001, Setup 0.002. Wooden Box Apple/Egg 0.3 and Screw/Board 0.5, ungated. Meso chance 0.6 and per-level amounts 1.5-2.5 x level. Reported here because it is the only placeholder file in item handling.

defects.title: Natural recovery placeholder blocks chair regeneration (owner: mechanics domain)
defects.detail: combat.json natural_recovery has hp_per_tick 10, tick_s 10 and delay_s 5. Any movement 'starts the 10 s again', which is a reset, but the brief requires a pause. It has no seated input. The chair bonus (522: additional 30 HP every 10 s, recovery.json stacks_with_natural_regen true) has nowhere to plug in until this is rewritten.

defects.title: KuroDB 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump' cannot be crosswalked by name
defects.detail: Hidden Street 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump 10%' maps solidly to MeowDB 177 (API: target Shoes, Jump +3, successRate 10). KuroDB's Orange Mushroom row 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump' (0.03% base, link 2040705) carries no success rate, and MeowDB has four Shoes Jump scrolls (174, 177, 180, 183). The chance should stay UNRESOLVED until KuroDB item 2040705 is read. Not on any progression path.

defects.title: Gender/id ambiguity for two Hidden Street (M)/(F) names
defects.detail: Blue Cloth Vest (M): npc-shops.html gives 949 (icon 1040011, male range), but a second 'Blue Cloth Vest' 958 is linked from item-db_960.html. Black Cloth Pants (F): 1179 is a candidate only by its position after 1177 and 1178 in item-db_1177.html's sibling list. The icon regex for item-page card lists is unreliable, because there the icon follows the link. Verify both on the item pages.

defects.title: Pistol has no weapon family even if MeowDB defines it
defects.detail: inventory.json weapon_subtypes and formulas/damage.json have no Gun or pistol family, and job_item_tags 'pirate' is a guess. If a manual search finds a MeowDB Pistol, it needs an adaptation entry. If not, it stays an HS-only unresolved member. Pirates are probably not in Classic.

defects.title: Item-side sources.monster_drops no longer describe runtime membership
defects.detail: Example: 522 still lists Snail (MeowDB community, disputed 1/1; gone from the 2026-10-05 live capture), and 541 lists Snail and Red Snail, while the Hidden Street lists differ. Nothing at runtime reads item sources. Keep them as MeowDB reference, and add a validator cross-check from each drop-table entry to its item id rather than rewriting the item files.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Manual MeowDB reads for the missing items (human, normal browser)
implementation_plan.detail:
Read in this order and save as dated captures under tools/meowdb/captures/items/<id>/ (item-db page text/HTML plus API JSON, with read_at):
(a) item-db/242 Green Apple, for Max per Stack, Untradeable and Where to buy.
(b) The 23 known ids: 944, 916, 625, 727, 721, 720, 650, 949, 958, 722, 1319, 717, 1435, 943, 951, 735, 617, 1318, 1170, 718, 672, 956, 1169, 1178, 1179, 680. 958 and 1178 are only there to settle the (M)/(F) gender question.
(c) MeowDB item-db searches for 'Pan Lid', 'Wooden Samurai Sword' (also try Katana or Samurai) and 'Pistol'. Record 'no result' as a capture too.
(d) Optional: the KuroDB item page for 2040705, to settle the Shoes Jump scroll chance.
No automated fetching.
implementation_plan.tests: none (source capture)

implementation_plan.step: 2. Make extraction reproducible from captures
implementation_plan.detail:
In lib.mjs fetchUrl, fall back to tools/meowdb/captures/<same cacheKey> before throwing, and record which source was used in field_sources. Fix the header comment so it matches the code.
In extract_items.mjs, derive the id set as: ITEM_IDS ∪ shops ∪ beginner ∪ every item id in quests (objectives, accept, rewards, random) ∪ breakable drops ∪ resolved crosswalk ids. Replace the 'delete unlisted files' step with a warning, so the 40 out-of-closure items stay (saves, recovery.json and tests use them).
For items whose API lacks slotMax and whose page is absent, emit a gap. A silent null must never become stack 1.
implementation_plan.tests: Re-run with an empty .cache restricted to the captured ids. Output must be byte-identical across two runs, and the existing 95 files unchanged.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Add the new canonical item files
implementation_plan.detail: Run the extractor to produce game/data/canonical/items/<id>.json for every resolved Hidden Street member: Green Apple 242 (Use/Food, mp_restore 30) plus whichever of the remaining 23-26 the reads confirm. Weapons need weapon blocks (two-handed Wooden Mallet and Metal Axe, Hardwood Wand, Crossbow with required ammunition 213, Garnier as a claw), and the Buckler goes to the shield slot. Do NOT create files for names with no MeowDB definition (Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword or Pistol, if absent) or for Omok Piece: Mushroom (D3-8).
implementation_plan.tests: Extend test_inventory_item_def.gd: 242 tab use, mp_flat 30, hp_flat 0, max_stack equal to the captured page value (not 1). Every new equip resolves equip_slot and, for weapons, ItemsConfig.weapon_subtype is non-empty.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Item crosswalk (shared with the drops domain)
implementation_plan.detail:
Create a reviewed crosswalk, e.g. game/data/canonical/drops/item_crosswalk.json, keyed by (monster, Hidden Street name). Each entry carries: meowdb_item_id or null, match kind (exact / normalized / alias / none), evidence, KuroDB name, link and raw value, and the decision.
Aliases with evidence:
- 'Arrow for Bow' / 'Arrow for Crossbow' are MeowDB's own /npc-shops spellings of 209 / 213.
- '(M)'/'(F)' is MeowDB's shop-list suffix (e.g. 'Grey Thick Sweat Pants (M)' = 1181), checked against the item's gender.
- 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump 10%' maps to 177 by target, stat and success rate.
- Jr. Sentinel Shellpiece maps to 347, not 2584 (quest 1005 reasoning).
- Omok Piece: Mushroom has no match (D3-8).
- KuroDB 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump' has no match (rate unknown).
Unresolved names use a non-typed key (hidden_street_name) so reference_checks and test_drops_data.gd:12 do not fail.
implementation_plan.tests: New validator check: every Hidden Street member is either resolved to an existing item or listed as unresolved with a reason. Every entry with chance > 0 resolves to a full item definition whose non-equip max_stack is not null.

implementation_plan.step: 5. Chair rules (pure core)
implementation_plan.detail:
Add game/scripts/core/items/chairs.gd (class Chairs):
- is_chair(def) = tab setup and setup_hp_bonus > 0.
- can_sit(character, item_id, ctx) returns ItemCodes results: owns the item, alive, grounded, not climbing, warping or knocked back. Add codes NOT_A_CHAIR and CANNOT_SIT_NOW to item_codes.gd.
- regen_per_tick(def) returns the bonus HP per setup_interval_s.
Add ItemDef.is_chair(). Add ItemService.sit(item_id) and stand(reason), emitting new Events signals sat_down(item_id) and stood_up(reason) (add both to events.gd).
implementation_plan.tests: New tests/unit/test_chairs.gd: 522 is a chair and 525 is a chair; potions are not. can_sit is refused while dead, airborne, climbing or without the item. sit emits sat_down; stand emits stood_up.

implementation_plan.step: 6. Seated player state and UI hooks
implementation_plan.detail:
In player_controller.gd, add a SEATED state (or a seated flag on GROUND). While seated, walk, jump, climb and attack are blocked. Any move, jump or attack key, damage, knockback, death, warp or map_left stands the player up. In player_visual.gd, add a seated pose and a chair prop.
In inventory_window.activate_slot, add a Setup branch that calls items.sit(), or stand() when already seated on that chair. Allow binding chairs to quickslots (MisoQuickslots.bind).
Remove 'sit' from controls_panel.gd NOT_AVAILABLE. Classic has no ground sit, so the sit key only stands up or re-uses the last chair; label this as an adaptation.
implementation_plan.tests: Update test_consumable_use.gd:97: 522 is still not a consumable, but a new test asserts that inventory_window.activate_slot on 522 sits the player. Add unit tests that movement or attack input while seated stands the player up, and that a map transition or teleport clears seated.

implementation_plan.step: 7. Seated regeneration (coordinate with the mechanics owner)
implementation_plan.detail: After natural_recovery.gd is changed to the owner rule (10 HP per 10 s of eligible time, a pause not a reset, eligible when standing still or seated, walk/jump/attack pausing), add the chair bonus. While seated on chair X, each eligible 10 s tick adds 10 + X.setup_hp_bonus, i.e. 40 HP with 522, clamped to Max HP. Record this as a labelled derivation (owner rule + recovery.json 'additional 30', stacks_with_natural_regen true; one shared timer chosen because MeowDB does not say). MP is not inferred.
implementation_plan.tests: Deterministic test: 10 s seated on 522 gives +40 HP; standing still gives +10; 6 s seated, 5 s walking, 4 s seated gives one tick; never above Max HP.

implementation_plan.step: 8. Persistence and real-game proof
implementation_plan.tests: New scenario passes via scripts/playtest.sh, and its report lands in _scratch/it3/.

implementation_plan.step: 9. Parity manifest rows for items
implementation_plan.detail: Generate the items section of maple_island_parity.json from the closure: 55 local, the new files, and unresolved names, plus the chair and mechanic rows listed here. Mark the 40 out-of-closure items as 'MeowDB reference only'. List inventory.json, drops.json and new_character.json values as deliberate adaptations.
implementation_plan.tests: A parity validator test: every quest, shop, box and drop item id appears as a row; no row is 'verified' without an evidence pointer.

implementation_plan.step: 10. Docs
implementation_plan.detail: Update docs/canonical/items.md: new items, captures as the source, crosswalk aliases, Green Apple MP, unresolved names. Update docs/runtime/ITEMS.md: Setup use, chairs, seated regen derivation, new result codes and signals. Update CONTENT_AUTHORING.md: how to add an item from a manual capture.
implementation_plan.tests: none

open_questions: Chair regeneration: is The Green Relaxer's 'additional 30 HP every 10 seconds' on the same 10 s timer as the owner's natural 10 HP/10 s (so 40 HP per 10 s seated), or on a separate timer? MeowDB is silent. The plan picks one shared timer and labels it.

Is there any sitting without a chair item? Rain's quiz (quest 1016, npcs/19.json) talks about 'chairs or benches around the map', but MeowDB's map data documents no bench objects on Maple Island. The plan does not invent map chairs. Does the project owner want the sit key to do anything without a chair?

Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword and Pistol: if MeowDB has no such item, do they stay permanent Hidden-Street-only unresolved members (the brief's 'missing probability stays visible' rule), or are they dropped from the table as not existing in Classic?
Omok Piece: Mushroom (KuroDB 1%): MeowDB's three candidates (486/495/498) are all 'Quest Item' with no drop sources. Keep it unresolved (D3-8), or does the owner want one chosen?
KuroDB 'Scroll for Shoes for Jump' (link 2040705, 0.03%): accept it as the chance for MeowDB 177, or leave it unresolved until the KuroDB item page is read?
Starter clothes at character creation: MeowDB does not document them (beginner.json starter_clothes null). Keep 'weapon only', or adopt the classic creation outfits as a labelled adaptation?

Should the 40 local items now outside the closure (ores, scrolls, higher-level gear, 525) stay as canonical files? The recommendation is yes, for save compatibility and formula/test references, marked as reference-only in parity.

summary:
Paths in defects and plan are relative to the repo root C:\Users\itech\.t3\worktrees\maplestory-isometric\t3code-d299c8ce.

STATS. Every stat of the 6 species in game/data/canonical/monsters/{1,2,3,4,5,9}.json matches the live MeowDB captures of 2026-10-05 (tools/meowdb/captures/monster_*.json|txt). I diffed every field with a script: level, HP, MP 30, EXP, touch estimate and base P.DMG, M.DMG, P.DEF, M.DEF (Red Snail 30), ACC (the COT2 values), AVOID, touch zone px, speed modifier and label, movement label, KB 1, Peace, element label, and every Maple Island spawn row (count, total, types, mob rate). The one real difference is a new published field: the live pages now show 'STAGGER 0.6 seconds - How long the mob is staggered for when knocked back' for all six species. The canonical records do not have this field. Four places still claim stagger time is unpublished: monsters/*.json gaps[], formulas/movement.json monster_knockback.gaps, misostory/combat.json monster_knockback.reason and docs/canonical/monsters.md. The runtime value is already right (0.6 s, measured in test_b check #42). It just comes from the hit1 clip through an adaptation rule. Orange Mushroom speed is NOT a mismatch: the live page shows 'Normal' with no number, which agrees with the cached 0 from the raw chunk.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE BASELINE test_b_combat FAILURE. No monster behind the player was hit. This is a test-harness defect, not a game defect. _reach_probes (test_b_combat.gd:1002-1030) places the player 0.75-1.4 m from the nearest Snail, facing away. It then counts 'hit': rec.has('mob') (line 1024), which is true when the attack hits ANY monster. On Snail Hunting Ground I there were 30 live Snails. The two 'behind_hit' records in _scratch/it3/baseline_playtests/test_b_combat/combat_samples.json (t=234.767 swingO1 and t=235.667 swingO2) have fwd_m +2.142 / +2.261 and lat_m -1.063 / -1.117. Those values come from the player's feet and facing captured at attack start, so the target was a second Snail IN FRONT and to the left. The probe Snail itself stayed about 1.34-1.40 m behind, almost exactly on the facing line (lateral about 0.03 m).
- Both hits are inside the canonical oracle. swingO1 mirrored reaches 18-88 px forward (0.45-2.20 m), and swingO2 reaches -5 to 73 px. The lateral band is ±(30 + 18.5) px = ±1.21 m.
- Check #22 confirms the game was right: 0 target mismatches over 214 attacks.
- Both records are the same Snail. The first hit pushed it 0.4 m away and provoked it, and it chased the player at 0.875 m/s. That predicts a position of (2.27, -1.13) m at the second attack; the record shows (2.261, -1.117).
- Geometrically, the farthest-behind Snail an attack can reach has its feet 23.5 px (0.59 m) behind the player: swingO2 reaches 5 px back, plus half the touch width.
- The Iteration Three log entry for the baseline (ITERATION_LOG.md:243) and the task's own baseline note ('hit a Snail behind the player') are misdiagnoses.
- The fix is to classify each probe by the hit target's identity and to re-check, before every tap, that no other monster is in reach in front.

BEHAVIOUR. Two movement models exist, matching the two documented labels:
- The five 'Stays on its floor' species are 3D random wanderers: a 60% chance of a new random heading after each stand, a ±50° jitter when turning, and a turn at ledges more than 0.45 m high. Their 'floor' is the whole mob region, so ramps let them change terraces.
- The Orange Mushroom hops (0.81 m up, 2 m down). Nothing ties its hops to 'a floor above or below its spawn point', so it can chain hops across terraces.
- All species share a 4 s provoked chase. The Peace rule (no touch damage until the Sentinel is hit) is implemented and checked in the real game. Its interpretation is still unverified.

HITBOXES. I found no invisible oversized contact-damage bubbles. Every species' touch-zone footprint is no larger than its measured model: the models are 1.06-1.54x wider (the Sentinel placeholder 1.68-1.86x). Contact happens at w/2 + 0.3 m player radius.
- The one invisible area favours the player. The 60 px attack depth plus a touch depth equal to the width gives a hit band of ±1.21 m (Snail) to ±1.54 m (Orange Mushroom) to each side, and AttackFx never draws it. It is documented, so I list it as an owner question, not a defect.
- Minor issues: the touch zones are square prisms, aligned to the monster's facing for contact but to the attacker's axes for attacks. The Orange Mushroom model's base sits 0.183 m above its feet. The Blue and Red Snail models are up to 1.5x wider than their hit boxes. The Tutorial Jr. Sentinel is still a grey procedural placeholder.
- When a hopping Orange Mushroom is hit, the hop overrides the push (WARN #43).

VERIFIED IN THE REAL GAME (test_b): contact damage windows, post-hit invulnerability, player knockback, KB threshold and stagger timing, push distance against the adaptation, death fade, EXP, target selection, and the Peace rule.

defects.title: test_b_combat reach probe counts hits on bystander Snails as 'behind' hits (baseline red); the game hit no monster behind the player
defects.detail: _reach_probes (game/tools/playtest/scenarios/test_b_combat.gd:1002-1030) takes the nearest Snail m (line 1012), places the player 0.75-1.4 m from it facing away (_stand_at toward=false, :941), taps attack (_tap_attack :983), and records 'hit': rec.has('mob') (:1024). That is true for a hit on ANY monster; _evaluate (:1276-1281) then fails on behind_hit > 0. In the baseline (seed 1, 000000040, 30 live Snails) both 'behind' hits (t=234.767 swingO1, t=235.667 swingO2) have fwd_m +2.142/+2.261 and lat_m -1.063/-1.117. _on_attack_resolved (:301-345) computes these from the player feet and facing captured at attack start, so the target was a second Snail in front and to the left. The probe Snail stayed about 1.34-1.40 m behind (lateral about 0.03 m). Both hits are canonical. swingO1 mirrored reaches 18-88 px (0.45-2.20 m), and the Snail's 37 px zone spans 1.68-2.60 m. swingO2 reaches -5 to 73 px (to 1.825 m), and the Snail's near edge is at 1.80 m. The lateral band is ±(30 + 18.5) px = ±1.21 m. Check #22 found 0 oracle mismatches over 214 attacks. Both records are the same Snail: it was pushed 0.4 m by the first hit, then chased the player (provoked_chase_s 4 s) at 0.875 m/s, which predicts (2.27, -1.13); observed (2.261, -1.117). The deepest possible 'behind' hit on a Snail has its feet 23.5 px (0.59 m) behind. The fights' minimum hit fwd was -0.13 m. The result depends on the seed and layout: the Iteration Two PLAYTHROUGH_REPORT had 18/18 behind whiffs over 3 seeds. ITERATION_LOG.md:243 ('an attack hit a Snail 0.75-1.4 m behind the player') is a misdiagnosis. FIX: (1) add rec['iid'] = actual_iid in _on_attack_resolved, store m.get_instance_id() in _reach_probes, and count behind_hit/far_hit only when the probe target itself was hit; record other hits as bystander_hit, which check #22 still covers. (2) Immediately before EVERY tap, require that no other live monster passes _oracle_overlap (:632) for any of the five Sword standing presentations at the current feet and facing. Otherwise re-place or choose another Snail, because a provoked bystander walks back into reach between taps.

defects.detail: The 2026-10-05 captures show 'STAGGER 0.6 seconds' for all six species. The canonical records have no field for it. Their gaps[] (e.g. canonical/monsters/2.json:793), formulas/movement.json:88 monster_knockback.gaps, misostory/combat.json:33 monster_knockback.reason and docs/canonical/monsters.md 'Gaps' all say the stagger duration is not published. The runtime derives 0.6 s from hit1 (CombatFormula.monster_stagger_s, combat_formula.gd:755-759), which is numerically correct, but the provenance is wrong. The extractor (tools/meowdb/extract_monsters.mjs:624) writes the stale gap text and does not read tools/meowdb/captures/.

defects.title: Orange Mushroom hops are not limited to 'a floor above or below its spawn point'
defects.detail: Monster._try_hop (monster.gd:333-367) measures rise and drop from the CURRENT position: rise up to 0.9 x 0.90 m apex = 0.81 m, drop up to hop_max_drop_m 2.0 m (misostory/monsters/9.json:17). The mob region is the whole map footprint (mob_region.gd). So repeated hops can carry it up or down any number of terraces, while MeowDB says 'Can hop to a floor above or below its spawn point'. No test covers spawn-relative floors.

defects.title: Floor walkers wander in random 3D headings and can leave their spawn floor by ramps
defects.detail: MonsterBrain._enter_walk (monster_brain.gd:148-153) re-rolls a uniformly random heading 60% of the time (_shared.json new_heading_chance 0.6); on_blocked reverses with ±50 deg jitter. The ledge test is ±0.45 m (monster.gd:307-310), and the region is the whole map footprint inset by 2 m. MeowDB: 'Walks back and forth on the floor it spawns on.' All five walkers share identical AI and differ only in idle/walk timings. This meets 'two documented styles' but only loosely matches 'back and forth' and 'its floor'.

defects.title: A knockback hit on a hopping Orange Mushroom loses or overrides the push
defects.detail: Monster.step (monster.gd:140-141) runs _step_push only when not airborne, while the brain's stagger timer keeps counting. The hop continues to its landing. test_b WARN #43: 3 of 139 knockback hits on airborne monsters moved them +0.543, -1.376 and -1.007 m, toward the attacker in two cases.

defects.title: Invisible, generous lateral attack band (isometric depth)
defects.detail: combat.json:73-74 attack_box_depth_px 60 (±0.75 m) plus a touch depth equal to the width hits monsters whose centre is up to ±(30 + w/2) px to the side: Sentinel ±1.01 m, Snail ±1.21 m, Blue/Red ±1.19 m, Shroom ±1.20 m, Orange Mushroom ±1.54 m. The player body is 0.6 m wide. AttackFx (attack_fx.gd:31-44) draws only an arc or spike along the facing line, so a bystander about 1.1 m to the side is hit by a slash that visibly misses it. It favours the player (not a contact bubble), and the adaptation is documented (verified:false), so the owner should decide.

defects.title: Square touch prisms are aligned differently for contact and attack, and corners protrude on diagonals
defects.detail: MeleeQuery.touch_overlaps (melee_query.gd:58-70) aligns the w x w footprint to the monster's facing. MeleeQuery.attack_hits (:30-36) aligns the same square to the attacker's forward and lateral axes. The corners reach sqrt2 x w/2 from the centre (Snail 0.65 m, Orange Mushroom 1.11 m) on round proxies. A disc of radius w/2 would be orientation-free and match the round models.

defects.title: Model visual bounds diverge from the canonical box (wide snails, floating Orange Mushroom)
defects.detail: test_b visual_fit (baseline report.md line 221): Blue Snail model 1.30x1.34 m and Red Snail 1.30x1.07 m vs a 0.875 m touch box (up to about 1.5x), so the visible shell edge can be whiffed (DEFERRED.md:28). The Orange Mushroom's lowest vertex is 0.183 m above its feet: at most 0.087 m of that is walk bob, so the proxy base is offset (creatures.py:319 sphere flatten_bottom 0.55; library height 1.1314 m fitted to 1.45 m). The fit is by height only (monster_visual.gd build). visual_fit is reported as a note, not a check.

defects.title: Some spawned monsters are unreachable for the combat bot (cross-reference to spawns and traversal)
defects.detail: test_b WARN #50: 8 targets skipped. 5 Tutorial Jr. Sentinels on 000000030 at local y 0.0 had the player 0.81-0.88 m above them (e.g. flat 2.01 m, dy -0.81). Only swingO2 (bottom +17 px) can reach a monster that low. The bot never got an attack in. Worth checking that Sentinel slots are on the walkable floor the player reaches.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Fix the test_b_combat reach probe (turns the baseline green) and correct the log
implementation_plan.detail: In game/tools/playtest/scenarios/test_b_combat.gd: (a) _on_attack_resolved (:301-345): add rec['iid'] = actual_iid to every hit and whiff record. (b) _reach_probes (:1002-1030): keep target_iid = m.get_instance_id(). Classify each probe as target_hit (rec.iid == target_iid), bystander_hit (any other hit) or whiff. Only target hits count as behind_hit/far_hit. (c) Add a pure helper _front_clear(feet, facing, level, exclude_iid) that returns false when any other live monster passes _oracle_overlap (:632) for any of the 5 Sword standing presentations (swingO1-3, stabO1-2). Call it right before EVERY _tap_attack. If it is not clear, re-place (retry _stand_at) or pick the next-nearest Snail. Count 'skipped_bystander' in the step detail. (d) _evaluate (:1276-1281): the check becomes 'the probe Snail behind / beyond reach is never hit'. Bystander hits are listed in the details and remain covered by check #22. (e) Fix docs/ITERATION_LOG.md:243 (the hits were on a bystander in front, fwd +2.14/+2.26 m, lat -1.06/-1.12 m; no monster behind was hit) and add the probe change to docs/runtime/PLAYTEST_HARNESS.md.
implementation_plan.tests: Unit test in test_playtest_b_oracles.gd for the classification and _front_clear helpers (a bystander inside swingO1's box makes the front not clear; a monster 1 m behind does not). Re-run ISOLATE=it3_b bash scripts/playtest.sh test_b_combat --seed 1, 2 and 3: #23 passes with behind_whiff >= 1 and behind_hit 0, and #22 stays at 0 mismatches.

implementation_plan.step: 2. Bring the published STAGGER into canonical data and drive the runtime from it
implementation_plan.detail: Add a capture reader to tools/meowdb/extract_monsters.mjs (cache-only; captures are local files). Parse 'STAGGER\n<n> seconds' from tools/meowdb/captures/monster_<id>.json|txt into stagger_ms (600) with field_sources {url, read_at, method: 'manual capture'}. Replace the gap text at :624 with 'knockback distance and speed are not published'. Regenerate game/data/canonical/monsters/*.json. Update extract_formulas.mjs so formulas/movement.json monster_knockback.gaps drops 'stagger duration'. Runtime: MonsterCombatStats gains stagger_ms. CombatFormula.monster_stagger_s prefers canonical stagger_ms, then the hit clip, then fallback_stagger_s. In combat.json set monster_knockback.stagger_duration to 'canonical_stagger' and rewrite the reason so only the 20 px distance stays an adaptation. Update docs/canonical/monsters.md (stat table gets a Stagger column; Gaps entry), MONSTERS_AND_COMBAT_RUNTIME.md and COMBAT.md.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Capture parity check so monster stats become provably 'verified'
implementation_plan.detail: Add tools/meowdb/check_captures.mjs, or an assertion pass inside extract_monsters.mjs, that compares every canonical monster field with its dated capture: level, HP, MP, EXP, touch estimate and base, M.DMG, P.DEF, M.DEF, ACC, AVOID, touch zone, speed label and number, movement label, KB, stagger, Peace and element label, plus each Maple Island spawn row (count, total, types, mob rate). Write a capture_check block {capture, read_at, fields_compared, result} into each canonical monster record, and list any difference in discrepancies[] with the dated capture winning. The script-based diff in this audit found no differences except stagger.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Spawn-floor-relative movement (jumper and, if the owner agrees, walkers)
implementation_plan.detail: Orange Mushroom: in monster.gd _try_hop (:333-367), also require the landing height to stay within one floor of home.origin.y: home.y - hop_max_drop_m <= y1 <= home.y + hop_max_rise_apex_fraction x hop_apex_m. Hops that would go further fail and the monster turns. New adaptation key in misostory/monsters/9.json, 'hop_floor_band': 'spawn_one_floor', with its reason. Walkers: an optional _shared.json key 'floor_band_m' (e.g. 0.6 m around home.y) checked in Monster.probe() as a new block reason 'floor', so 'Stays on its floor' means the spawn floor, not any ramp-connected terrace. Optionally lower new_heading_chance for walkers so they pace back and forth (owner decision).

implementation_plan.step: 5. Consistent knockback for a monster hit mid-hop
implementation_plan.detail: In Monster.receive_hit, when res.knockback and _hop is active, cut the hop's horizontal travel: turn it into a fall from the current point (vertical_speed from the arc) and let _step_push run during the fall, or postpone the stagger push to landing with the full 20 px. Choose one and document it in combat.json monster_knockback, since KB in the air is unpublished.

open_questions: Lateral attack band: keep attack_box_depth_px 60 (hits monsters whose centre is up to ±1.21 m (Snail) / ±1.54 m (Orange Mushroom) to the side, beyond the slash the player sees) or narrow it toward the 0.6 m player body width? Either way, should AttackFx draw the band?
Should 'Stays on its floor' bind walkers to their spawn floor in 3D (a floor_band around the spawn height), or is any ramp-connected terrace in the mob region acceptable?
Should walkers pace 'back and forth' (a persistent axis, 180-degree turns) instead of re-rolling a random heading 60% of the time after each stand?
Interpretation of 'Can hop to a floor above or below its spawn point': exactly one floor relative to the spawn height, or one floor per hop relative to the current position (the current behaviour)?
Knockback of a monster hit mid-hop: cancel the hop and fall with the push, or apply the full push on landing? MeowDB publishes neither.
The Peace interpretation (the Sentinel touches for 1 once provoked, chases 4 s) stays verified:false: should Iteration Three keep it, or make the Sentinel never touch?
Should the new STAGGER field be brought in by an extractor step that reads tools/meowdb/captures/ (recommended), or by a hand-patched canonical field with provenance?

summary:
CANONICAL PARITY OF COUNTS IS EXACT. All 25 maps have 577 spawn points across 51 species-map rows. All 51 rows in the live 2026-10-05 captures (tools/meowdb/captures/monster_{1,2,3,4,5,9}) match game/data/canonical/maps/*.json exactly on count, share denominator, number of types, mob rate and "~7.5s". The runtime makes exactly one SpawnSlot per MeowDB spawns[i], keeping its index (map_definitions.gd:684). test_spawn_slots.gd:19-31 asserts the per-species counts against canonical data for all 25 maps (total 577).

TIMING AND CAPACITY ARE CENTRALIZED AND TESTED. Two pure classes hold every number and read it from formulas/spawn_rate.json: SpawnModel (spawn_model.gd) and MapInstanceState (map_instance_state.gd). The rules are a 7.56 s global tick, a 5 s wave cooldown, a respawn on the first tick at or after death + cooldown, and capacity floor(points x 75%) solo. Unit tests cover them: test_spawn_model.gd:39-88 checks every map's capacity against MeowDB's own capacity_solo estimate (426 island total), and test_map_instance_state.gd covers the state rules. The real game also checks them: test_b_combat rows 48 and 49 (52 refills, all on a tick; capacity 4/6, 30/40, 31/42, 28/38 on 030, 040, 050 and 1020). No arbitrary Iteration Two delays remain. The first fill to capacity is a documented adaptation (MAP_ARCHITECTURE open question 6).

MOB RATE. Re-reading the cache gives three answers:
- Spawn speed: no MeowDB source has mob rate change it. Every live row shows RESPAWN "~7.5s" at 0.6x, 1.0x, 1.2x, 1.3x and 1.5x alike. The monster-page tooltip says "Not applied to the respawn figures yet."
- Capacity: MeowDB contradicts itself.
  - The mechanics pages say ignored. The guide (Updated 2026-08-24): "Each map's data carries a spawn-rate multiplier, typically between 0.8 and 2.0. Other MapleStory servers multiplied map capacity by it. MSC does not. The live game ignores it; capacity comes only from spawn-point count and the player scalar." The glossary (page updated 2026-09-04, the most recently dated page): "There is no separate map-wide multiplier or fixed 40-mob cap." formulas/spawns: "Capacity = floor(SpawnPoints × PlayerScalar)", with no mob-rate term.
  - The display pages say it multiplies capacity. Map page 000000050: "Mob rate multiplies how many monsters this map keeps alive at once. This map has 42 spawn points and a mob rate of 1.5x, so expect about 63 monsters up at a time instead of 42. The spawn figures above do not apply it yet. This is our best reading from closed-beta play, where a high-rate map held far more monsters than it has spawn points; an exact whole-map count has not been done." Monster tooltip: "Multiplier on how many monsters that map keeps alive at once, on top of its spawn-point count. Above 1.0 means a fuller map."
- What tips the balance: the display reading contradicts the page's own player scalar. 000000040 says "capacity is ~30 concurrent mobs solo" and also "its 40 spawn points are the whole story: about 40 monsters up at a time". Its numbers (63, 86, 52, 41) also exceed the spawn-point count, which the one-monster-per-slot runtime cannot represent at all.

Verdict: mob rate scales nothing in MeowDB's documented mechanics, and if it did scale anything it would be capacity, never speed. Keep "ignored", but record it as a MisoStory decision between conflicting MeowDB pages. Iteration Two stated it as a fact ("MSC ignores mobRate", MAP_ARCHITECTURE 3.2, ITERATION_LOG R2-4). The promised "one config switch" (maps.md:184) does not exist. The flag is read from canonical data (applied_by_msc), and the path is dead: map_instance_state.gd:58 and map_definitions.gd:125 never pass mob_rate.

CANONICAL VS MISOSTORY SEPARATION holds. Species, count and mobTime come from canonical; position, region and placement come from sidecar spawn_regions and presentation.json/maps overrides. Two exceptions: the mob-rate interpretation lives in canonical data, and MeowDB's per-spawn x_px/y_px are not used at all. The tier mapping in MAP_ARCHITECTURE 4.7.1 step 2 was never built. Slots go to Blender v8-era species-tagged regions in proportion to area.

PLACEMENT ADAPTATION IS PARTIAL.
- Done and verified with physics (test_world_static.gd:101-130): grounded, capsule-clear (walls), inside the mob region, at least 4 m from every arrival and player_spawns[0], at least 1.2 m apart, outside keep-outs.
- Missing:
  - NPC clearance. The avoid list at spawn_slot_planner.gd:39-44 is portals plus player_spawns[0] only. Sam stands inside 000000040's Snail_3 region (4 slots). Mai is 1.6 m and Maria 3.2 m from 000000050 regions, against an NPC interaction radius of 1.6 m.
  - Player-overlap avoidance at respawn (map_instance_view.gd:177-181).
  - A reachability check.
  - Density control. Static emulation shows clumps such as Tomato Field BlueSnail_7 5 slots/16 m², 000001014 BlueSnail_1 7 slots/41 m² and 000001006 RedSnail_10 6 slots/30 m².
- MapKit.mobs() drops its avoid zones from the exported regions (mapkit.py:979-995; 33 of 177 calls, e.g. A Split Road's plaza).

WOODEN BOX PLACEMENTS ARE MISSING. Canonical data has 19 placements (000001000 x5 with respawn 120/120/120/180/90 s, 000001010 x6, 000001011 x2, 000001012 x2, 000001013 x1, 000001014 x3, all at 120 s). There are no sidecar markers, no authoring API, no runtime slot or state, and no actor.

defects.title: MeowDB relative spawn positions are unused; the 4.7.1 tier mapping was never built
defects.detail: spawns[i].x_px/y_px are dropped at map_definitions.gd:684-691. The planner assigns slots by species tag and region area only (largest remainder), so per-platform composition follows Blender's v8-era m.mobs layout rather than MeowDB. MAP_ARCHITECTURE 4.7.1 step 2 describes a tier projection the code does not implement; the planner's own header calls it 'simplified'.

defects.title: Spawn clumping in small species-tagged regions
defects.detail: Region weight is area_m2, because spawn_regions carry 'proxies' rather than 'points' (map_definitions.gd:777). Static emulation of _assign_areas gives Tomato Field BlueSnail_7 5 slots/16 m2, BlueSnail_5 3/10 m2, RedSnail_9 4/14 m2; 000001005 BlueSnail_5 5/23 m2; 000001014 BlueSnail_1 7/41 m2 (6 Orange Mushroom); 000001006 RedSnail_10 6/30 m2; 000001004 Snail_1 10/40 m2. The only density rule is 1.2 m minimum spacing.

defects.title: Blender mobs() avoid zones are not exported with the spawn region
defects.detail: MapKit.mobs passes avoid only to the proxy scatter, then calls spawn_region(area) with the full polygon (mapkit.py:979-995). 33 of 177 mobs() calls are affected: the A Split Road plaza (m50000 lines 339-343) and the Snail Garden bed_avoid strips are non-colliding zones the runtime capsule cannot see; Dangerous Forest tracks, glade_clear and g1_clear; Mid Forest dip_clear and t0_clear.

defects.title: No reachability guarantee for spawn slots
defects.detail: Slots are checked for ground, clearance and region but not for connection to the walkable traversal graph. 'relaxed' placement accepts any top surface in the area. test_b row 50 WARN: 8 monsters skipped (5 Sentinels on 000000030, 1 Shroom on 000000050 with dy 3.0 m) after two 4 s approaches. Likely a bot limitation, but unverified.

defects.title: Stale planner comment
defects.detail: spawn_slot_planner.gd:6-8 says 000000030 has no spawn areas. Its sidecar now exports 4 authored spawn_regions (ValleyEast_G5, Hilltop_G3, HighTerrace_M3, Ledge_M1).

defects.title: No automated check that canonical spawn rows match the dated live captures
defects.detail: test_spawn_slots compares against the cached maps/*.json only. The 2026-10-05 captures happen to match all 51 rows today (manual node comparison), but nothing guards future re-extractions or captures.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Record the mob-rate decision and make the switch real
implementation_plan.detail: Add a misostory adaptation key (game/data/misostory/presentation.json spawns.apply_map_mob_rate, default false, with a reason quoting the guide, glossary, map-page and tooltip readings, and verified:false). SpawnModel takes the switch from WorldTuning/misostory data instead of using the canonical applied_by_msc as its switch; keep the canonical field as the guide statement. Plumb def.environment_configuration.mob_rate into MapInstanceState.fresh()/fresh_for() and MapDefinitions.capacity_of(). While the slot model is one monster per point, cap the result at the point count and log a warning when the multiplied value would exceed it. Update MAP_ARCHITECTURE 3.2, ITERATION_LOG and docs/canonical/maps.md discrepancy 1 (cite the 2026-10-05 live MOB RATE column and the tooltip) so they state a decision, not a fact.
implementation_plan.tests: test_spawn_model.gd: replace the canonical-flag pin (line 27) with switch-off and switch-on cases (000000050 gives 31 off; switch on gives min(floor(31 x 1.5), 42) = 42 plus a warning); test_map_instance_state.gd: fresh() reads the map's mob_rate only when the switch is on

implementation_plan.step: 2. Guard canonical spawn rows against the dated live captures
implementation_plan.detail: Add a cache-only check (node, tools/meowdb) that parses captures/monster_*.json maple_island_map_rows and monster_2.txt and asserts count, share denominator, types, mob rate and '~7.5s' against game/data/canonical/maps/*.json (51 rows). Feed the result into the parity manifest's population rows.
implementation_plan.tests: Script exits non-zero on any of the 51 rows differing; run it in CI / validate_data

implementation_plan.step: 3. NPC clearance for spawn slots
implementation_plan.detail: Add presentation.json spawns.slot_npc_clearance_m (for example npc.interaction_radius_m 1.6 + clearance_radius_m 0.35 + a margin, about 2.5 m, with a reason). In SpawnSlotPlanner.plan add every def.npc_definitions[].transform.origin to a second avoid set scored like the arrivals. Reuse the existing scoring and 'forced' warning path rather than inventing a new keep-out system. Optionally add NPC discs to MobRegion only if playtests show wandering monsters crowding NPCs (classic monsters walk past NPCs).
implementation_plan.tests: test_spawn_slots.gd: new test_slots_keep_clear_of_npcs (flat GroundQuery); test_world_static.gd: assert every slot is at least slot_npc_clearance_m from every NPC on all 25 maps (000000040 Sam, 000000050 Mai/Maria, 000000030 Todd/Peter)

implementation_plan.step: 4. Never realize a respawn inside the player
implementation_plan.detail: In MapInstanceView._process/_spawn, before realizing slot i, check the player's feet against the slot (new presentation.json spawns.respawn_player_clearance_m, for example 1.5 m, documented as an adaptation: classic MS does not guarantee this). If it is too close, keep the index at the back of the queue and retry each frame until the player leaves. MapInstanceState stays pure and the state's alive count and capacity are unchanged. Give the view a player-position Callable, set by MonsterSystem.
implementation_plan.tests: test_map_instance_view.gd: a respawn under the player is deferred, then realized once the player moves away; real game: tighten test_b_combat check 39 to fail on any realized monster within the clearance

implementation_plan.step: 5. Export Blender avoid zones with spawn regions
implementation_plan.detail: In MapKit.mobs pass avoid into spawn_region and store it as exclusions (exclude_xz polygons/discs) in spawn_regions_json. Have the exporter write them, MapDefinitions._parse_area read them, and SpawnSlotPlanner treat them as keep-outs (same in_keepout path). This is a source-world change, so re-export the affected maps (000000050, 000001002, 000001003, 000001004, 000001005, 000001006).
implementation_plan.tests: validate.py: exclusions round-trip; test_world_static.gd: no slot inside a region exclusion; test_spawn_slots deterministic test still passes

implementation_plan.step: 6. Density and composition rules (topology-aware distribution)
implementation_plan.detail: Add a density cap (presentation.json spawns.max_slots_per_m2 or min area per slot): when a region's quota exceeds it, spill to the next species-tagged region, then to untagged ones. Optionally implement MAP_ARCHITECTURE 4.7.1 step 2 for maps whose 2D layout matches v8 (topology_diff: not 000000001/020/042/1021): fit a px-to-local transform per map from portals that have both MeowDB x_px/y_px and 3D anchors, project each spawns[i] and prefer the nearest species-tagged region. Put per-map reasons and pins in game/data/misostory/maps/<id>.json (spawn_region_quota / spawn_slot_overrides).
implementation_plan.tests: test_spawn_slots.gd: no region exceeds the density cap; each slot's region carries its species tag; per-map counts still equal canonical; quotas are deterministic

implementation_plan.step: 7. Spawn reachability check
implementation_plan.detail: Using the Phase 13 walkable-surface graph / flood fill (game/tools/traversal_*.gd), assert every slot's ground point is in the component reachable from player_spawns[0] and the portal arrivals. Also report placement-mode counts (strict/relaxed/pinned) per map in the debug report and review each relaxed slot.
implementation_plan.tests: New test_spawn_reachability.gd (INCLUDE_WORLD=1): 577 slots reachable; relaxed count recorded

implementation_plan.step: 8. Wooden Box placements and respawn
implementation_plan.detail: Blender: add a MapKit.reactor(index, x, y) marker API and place the 19 boxes in m1000000, m1010000, m1010001, m1010002, m1010003 and m1010004 following MeowDB relative x_px/y_px. Have the exporter write sidecar reactors[] with the canonical index. Runtime: MapDefinitions builds ReactorSlot entries (index, breakable id 0000001, respawn_s per placement from the canonical map, which keeps 90/120/180 on 000001000), grounded and kept clear of portals and NPCs. Extend MapInstanceState with reactor slots {alive, hits, broken_at}: respawn at broken_at + respawn_s; whether it also waits for the 7.56 s tick is a labelled adaptation in misostory data, since MeowDB is silent. Snapshot with the map like monster slots; never saved. The breakable actor (4 hits, drops) belongs to the breakables/drops plan.
implementation_plan.tests: test_reactor_slots.gd: 19 slots (5/6/2/2/1/3) with per-placement respawn_s; test_map_instance_state.gd: reactor respawn timing; test_world_static.gd: reactors grounded, clear, away from portals and NPCs; validate.py: reactor marker count parity

implementation_plan.step: 9. Real-game population check on all 15 hunting maps and the parity manifest
implementation_plan.detail: Add a playtest scenario (or extend test_b_combat) that warps through all 15 monster maps. It asserts live count == solo capacity after first fill and after kills, refills only on ticks, the long-run species mix of live monsters matches canonical slot shares, and no realized monster lies within the NPC, arrival or player clearance. Do the same for reactors on the 6 maps. Emit population:<map>, mechanic:spawn-* and breakable-placement:<map> rows into MAPLE_ISLAND_PARITY.md / maple_island_parity.json.
implementation_plan.tests: Playtest report rows per map; parity manifest states move to verified

implementation_plan.step: 10. Housekeeping
implementation_plan.detail: Fix the stale 000000030 comment at spawn_slot_planner.gd:6-8. Document the respawn slot-selection adaptation (uniform among eligible dead slots, MeowDB gap) in MAP_ARCHITECTURE 4.7.2 and give it an owner-visible note.
implementation_plan.tests: none (docs)

open_questions: Mob rate: the owner must confirm 'ignored' (MeowDB guide 2026-08-24, glossary page 2026-09-04, formula page) or adopt the map-page reading (capacity x mob rate: about 4 on 000000030, 63 on 000000050, 86 on 000001000, 52 on 000001001, 41 on 000001014). The second reading exceeds the spawn-point count, so the one-monster-per-slot model would need multi-occupancy or synthetic slots.
Player-overlap avoidance is not classic behaviour. Is deferring the realization (as in plan step 4) acceptable, or should the tick pick a different eligible slot?
Respawn slot selection: keep uniform among all eligible dead slots (a killed spot waited up to 197 s in test_b) or prefer the just-killed slot? MeowDB lists selection order as a gap.
Wooden Box respawn: exact per-placement respawn_s (90/120/180 on 000001000), or aligned to the 7.56 s global tick? The breakable page shows a single 120 s per map.

Placement-mode counts (strict/relaxed/pinned) and actual slot coordinates were not dumped; a Godot run is needed to confirm that NPC proximity (Sam/Mai/Maria) materializes and whether relaxed slots sit on prop tops.
Should MeowDB x_px/y_px drive 3D placement on maps whose 2D layout matches v8, given that topology_diff says not to project px onto 000000001/020/042/1021?
Should NPC clearance also restrict monster wandering (MobRegion discs), or only spawn points? Classic monsters walk past NPCs.
