summary:
Audited at HEAD 54e04dc. Four commits landed during the audit: 74a89d1 (Hidden Street captures, now tracked), 679297c (MeowDB capture of Green Apple 242 and Omok 486/495/498), d85a1a1 (iteration log decisions D3-1 to D3-8) and 54e04dc (quest 1008 spot check). All counts below describe that state.

CURRENT STATE: the whole drop pipeline runs on Iteration Two placeholders.
- Membership comes from MeowDB's community lists in game/data/canonical/drops/<owner>.json. D3-6 replaced this source with the Hidden Street (HS) lists.
- Every chance, quantity and meso value comes from game/data/misostory/drop_rates.json, which labels them all canonical:false / verified:false.
- DropRates (drop_rates.gd) resolves rates by type and subtype. DropRoller is pure and seeded but has no quest context.
- The loot actors and the meso pickup, display and save path are complete and proven in the real game (test_d_inventory steps 21-23, 59, 70).
- No drop entry records membership_source or chance_source. provenance_checks.gd:18-22 accepts only MeowDB as an authority.
- Nothing reads the KuroDB or HS captures. There is no crosswalk, no raw-value parser and no quest gating.
- The Wooden Box has complete canonical data (4 hits, 19 placements on 6 maps, per-placement respawn) but no runtime at all. Quest 1012 (Pio: 3 Rusty Screw + 3 Old Wooden Board, whose only source is the box) cannot be completed in the real game. This is a blocker.

PROPOSED TABLE (full detail in domain_data):
- 71 HS members across the 6 monsters.
- 14 are fully resolved: KuroDB chance plus a local MeowDB item.
  - 347 at 1.0 (Kuro 'Quest 1035').
  - 348, 349, 350, 351, 356 at 1.0.
  - Red Potion 270 at 0.02 on 5 monsters.
  - Brown Woodsman Boots 1325, Brown Hard Leather Boots 1314 and Red Ninja Sandals 1327 at 0.0008 each.
- 4 rows have a KuroDB chance but no item file: Green Apple 242 at 0.02 on Snail, Blue Snail, Shroom and Red Snail. 242 exists only in tools/meowdb/captures/items_api.json.
- 1 row has a chance but an ambiguous item: Omok Piece : Mushroom at 0.01, MeowDB 486/495/498 (D3-8).
- 52 rows have no KuroDB chance. One of them, Scroll for Shoes for Jump 10% = MeowDB 177, has a Kuro candidate at 0.0003 that is ambiguous and stays unresolved until Kuro item 2040705 is checked. Five of the 52 have no MeowDB item, or an ambiguous one: Pan Lid, Wooden Samurai Sword, Pistol, and the gender-suffixed Cloth Vest/Pants.
- 62 Kuro-only rows are excluded.
- Today about 66 MeowDB-sourced item rows roll at placeholder rates and must stop. Examples: Bronze Ore, Garnet Ore, Sword and Green Headband on the Snail; Iron Ore and Razor on the Blue Snail; Arrows at 0.02 everywhere.

MESOS: the amount comes from MeowDB for the Snail (2) and from HS otherwise (Blue Snail 4, Shroom 4-6, Red Snail 8-12, Orange Mushroom 9-13). The chance is KuroDB 40% ('40% base | Meso drop') for all five. The Tutorial Jr. Sentinel drops no mesos (no Kuro row; HS '?'). The Snail discrepancy (HS says 1) is recorded, and MeowDB's dropChancePct 100 is a form constant that must never be used as a chance. Current placeholders: chance 0.6 and per-level amounts 3-5, 4-8, 6-10, 12-20. Expected mesos per kill fall: Snail 1.2→0.8, Blue Snail 2.4→1.6, Shroom 3.6→2.0, Red Snail 4.8→4.0, Orange Mushroom 9.6→4.4.

WOODEN BOX:
- Old Wooden Board and Rusty Screw: 'Chance value 1 | Quest 1008' → 1.0 under the 1/N interpretation, gated on MeowDB quest 1012 (inferred).
- Apple: 'Chance value 4' → 0.25.
- Egg: unresolved. It is not needed by any quest.

PROGRESSION-REQUIRED DROPS are all resolved under the new sources: 347, 349, 356 (quests), 348/349/351 (Three Snails), and 441/442 once the box runtime exists. The only progression blocker is the missing breakable runtime.

GAMEPLAY IMPACT, to re-measure but NOT to re-tune: every kill gives one leftover shell or cap, mesos fall 35-55%, and nearly all equipment drops disappear (only 3 boot/sandal items at 0.08%). Expect test_c_progression and test_d_inventory meso and loot budgets to shift.

defects.title: Wooden Box has no runtime, so Pio's quest 1012 cannot be completed
defects.detail: Quest 1012 needs 3 Rusty Screw (441) and 3 Old Wooden Board (442). Their only source is the Wooden Box (MeowDB breakable 0000001; KuroDB reactor 2001). The canonical record and the 19 placements exist, but there is no actor, isometric placement, hit handling, break, respawn, state or loot trigger. test_drops_data.test_quest_items_are_obtainable passes only because DropRoller can roll owner 0000001 in isolation. The brief forbids faking it by granting the items. DEFERRED.md:16-17 confirms the gap.

defects.title: All drop chances, quantities and meso values are Iteration Two placeholders, and membership is the superseded MeowDB community list
defects.detail: drop_rates.json drives every rolled value (type/subtype defaults, owner overrides, mesos.chance 0.6, per_level 1.5/2.5). This fails DoD 'no placeholder monster item-drop chances' and the meso rules. Under D3-6 about 56 non-member items roll today, for example Snail 320/413/541/709/713/933/939/940 and Blue Snail 321/414/558/934/935/937/939/945/960/963/1157/1181/1440. About 10 HS members with no KuroDB chance also roll today (209/213 on every monster, 715 on the Blue Snail). Full lists are in domain_data monsters.*.remove_from_runtime_not_hs_member and stop_dropping_hs_member_unresolved.

defects.title: Green Apple (242) has a resolved KuroDB chance on 4 monsters but no canonical item definition
defects.detail: HS and KuroDB both list Green Apple ('2.00% base | Qty 1') for the Snail, Blue Snail, Shroom and Red Snail. MeowDB 242 exists only as a preview API body in tools/meowdb/captures/items_api.json (Use/Food, 'Restores 30 MP', price 3, iconKey 2010007). It has no item-db page in the cache, so sell-price basis, max_stack, tradeable and the consumable block's provenance are gaps. Without a game/data/canonical/items/242.json these 4 rows must stay non-rolling ('resolved chance, missing definition').

defects.title: No quest-gated drops
defects.detail: The Kuro rows that matter carry '| Quest N': Jr. Sentinel Shellpiece 'Quest 1035', and Board/Screw 'Quest 1008' on reactor 2001. DropRoller.roll(owner_id, db, rng) (drop_roller.gd:21) has no quest context, and MonsterSystem.on_monster_died passes none (monster_system.gd:217). The Kuro-to-MeowDB quest mapping (1035->1005, 1008->1012) is inferred from item-need uniqueness and is not recorded anywhere. Two tests assume ungated drops: test_drops_roller.gd:61-66 and :81-84, and test_drops_data.gd:90-98 _obtainable.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Reviewed crosswalk and offline join
implementation_plan.detail: Create tools/drops/crosswalk.json, checked in and reviewed. Per monster, map each HS member name to {meowdb_item_id | meowdb_candidates[], meowdb_match: exact|normalized|alias-with-evidence|ambiguous|none, evidence}. Map each HS name to its Kuro row {kuro_name, kuro_item_id, kuro_match, evidence}. Add a quests block: kuro 1035->meowdb 1005 and kuro 1008->meowdb 1012, both with basis 'item-need uniqueness'. Seed it with the table in domain_data. Create tools/drops/join.mjs, pure and offline. It reads only tools/hiddenstreet/captures, tools/kurodb/captures, tools/meowdb/captures and game/data/canonical/items, and refuses any network access. Call it from tools/meowdb/extract_monsters.mjs buildDropTable (l.724) so one writer produces drops/<owner>.json. MeowDB's community and MSEA lists move to meowdb_reference.entries unchanged. Fail hard on any HS name missing from the crosswalk and on any Kuro row that is neither matched nor listed as excluded.
implementation_plan.tests: Run the extractor twice and diff: the output must be byte-identical. A node self-check in join.mjs asserts member counts 1/11/12/15/15/17 and excluded counts 0/7/13/10/18/14.

implementation_plan.step: 2. Drop record schema v2
implementation_plan.detail:
Each drops/<owner>.json gets these fields:
- entries[]: one row per HS member (box: MeowDB member) with:
  - item_id: a local MeowDB id, or null
  - meowdb_item_id / meowdb_candidates
  - hs_name, hs_categories
  - membership_source {authority:'Hidden Street (Before Chaos, GMS v0.96)' | 'MeowDB MS Classic', url, read_at, raw_value (verbatim HS line), version_note}
  - chance_source {authority:'KuroDB', url, read_at, site_updated:'Updated 10/2/2026', kuro_item_id, kuro_name, match_method, raw_value, format:'kuro_monster_pct'|'kuro_reactor_chance_value', numerator, denominator, normalized_probability, conversion ('p/100' or '1/N, interpretation')}, or null
  - quantity {min, max, source: Kuro 'Qty n', or 'assumption 1' for reactors}
  - quest_gate {kuro_quest_id, meowdb_quest_id, basis}, or null
  - status: resolved | unresolved_chance | unresolved_item | resolved_missing_definition
  - notes
- kuro_only_excluded[]: verbatim Kuro rows with reason 'not on Hidden Street list'.
- meso:
  - amount {min, max, authority MeowDB|Hidden Street, raw_value, url, read_at, distribution:'uniform_integer_inclusive (MisoStory interpretation)'}
  - chance {authority KuroDB, raw_value '40% base | Meso drop', normalized 0.4}, or {status:'none', reason:'no KuroDB Mesos row'}
  - discrepancies[] (Snail: HS 1; report dropChancePct 100 not a rate)
- sources{} block with the verbatim HS lines and Kuro rows, so Godot tests can re-derive everything without reading tools/.
The Wooden Box record keeps MeowDB membership, uses the reactor format, and leaves Egg unresolved.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Green Apple item record
implementation_plan.detail: Add game/data/canonical/items/242.json, built from tools/meowdb/captures/items_api.json by extract_items.mjs reading captures, or hand-authored with a source block. Fields: Use/Food, consumable mp +30, npc price 3, icon 2010007. Declare gaps for sell-price basis, max_stack and tradeable. Do not create files for ambiguous or unknown items; keep their candidates on the entry.
implementation_plan.tests: test_drop_tables_sources: every resolved entry's item_id exists; 242 is a valid consumable.

implementation_plan.step: 4. DropChance parser (GDScript)
implementation_plan.detail: New game/scripts/core/drops/drop_chance.gd (class DropChance). It has parse_kuro_monster(raw), parse_kuro_reactor(raw) and parse_meowdb_meso_report(rep). parse_kuro_monster returns {ok, p, numerator, denominator, qty, quest, meso, error}. It uses integer numerator/denominator from the decimal string, so '0.0700' -> 700/1000000, with no float truncation. Bounds: 0 < p <= 1. It rejects negative values, values over 100%, an empty percent, and the 'Chance value' format passed to the percent parser (and vice versa). parse_kuro_reactor returns 1/N with conversion 'reciprocal (interpretation)' and requires N >= 1. The meso-report parser returns amounts only and always reports chance:null.
implementation_plan.tests:
game/tests/unit/test_drop_chance_parse.gd covers:
- '26% base | Qty 1' -> 0.26
- '2.00% base | Qty 1' -> 0.02 (not 2.0, not 0.0002)
- '0.0700% base | Qty 1' -> 0.0007
- '0.0800%' -> 0.0008
- '0.90%' -> 0.009 (not 0, not 0.9)
- '12.50%' -> 0.125
- '100% base' and '100.00% base | Qty 1 | Quest 1035' -> 1.0 with quest 1035
- '40% base | Meso drop' -> meso 0.4
- 'Chance value 4' -> 0.25 and 'Chance value 1 | Quest 1008' -> 1.0 with quest
- 'Chance value 0', '-5% base', '150% base', '' and 'abc' are rejected
- MeowDB report {dropChancePct:100} never yields a chance

implementation_plan.step: 5. Resolver, roller and quest context
implementation_plan.detail: Rewrite DropRates.effective_entries to read entry.chance_source.normalized_probability. A row is runtime-eligible only if status is resolved, item_id is local and the chance is in (0,1]. Every other row stays in the output with chance 0 and excluded set to its status (unresolved_chance, unresolved_item or missing_definition), so it remains visible. Rewrite meso_rule to read meso.amount and meso.chance (Sentinel: none). Reduce game/data/misostory/drop_rates.json to a labelled debug knob (global_rate_multiplier 1.0) plus the documented interpretations (meso range distribution, reactor 1/N, quest-gating semantics). Delete type_rates, subtype_rates, default_rate, owner overrides, mesos.chance and per_level. Change the signature to DropRoller.roll(owner_id, db, rng, ctx := {}), where ctx.active_quests is a PackedStringArray. A gated entry rolls only when its meowdb_quest_id is active, and it still consumes one randf() so seeds stay stable. MonsterSystem.on_monster_died (l.217) passes the active quests from the quest engine (QuestEngine.active_quests). Update the debug 'drops' command text (debug_commands.gd:66, 614) and add a 'drops unresolved' listing.

implementation_plan.step: 6. Validation and provenance
implementation_plan.detail:
Add game/scripts/core/validation/drop_table_checks.gd and hook it into the validation runner. Errors:
- a runtime-eligible entry whose item_id is not local
- a normalized_probability that differs from DropChance.parse(raw_value)
- a probability outside (0,1]
- an entry whose membership_source.authority is not the decided authority for its owner kind
- an entry whose raw HS name is absent from sources.hidden_street lines
- a Kuro row that is neither matched nor excluded
- a Kuro-only row present in entries
Warnings, always listed:
- each unresolved entry
- each ambiguous crosswalk row
- the Snail meso discrepancy
- the box respawn discrepancy
In provenance_checks.gd, allow per-field authorities from an allow-list (MeowDB MS Classic, Hidden Street (Before Chaos), KuroDB). Non-MeowDB entries need url, read_at, raw_value and verified:false. Teach build_sources_index.mjs to emit per-record authorities and regenerate canonical_sources.json. Generate a provenance validation report (Phase 17) listing, for each owner, which authority supplies drops.membership, drops.probability, mesos.amount and mesos.probability. reference_checks: validate meowdb_candidates only as reference (no error).
implementation_plan.tests: test_data_validation_* extended. Canonical validation (scripts/validate_data.sh) must report 0 errors, with the unresolved drops present as warnings.

implementation_plan.step: 7. Drop policy tests
implementation_plan.detail:
New game/tests/unit/test_drop_tables_sources.gd covers:
- (a) Kuro-only excluded: for each owner, no entry name or id is in kuro_only_excluded, and the planted example 'Snail Card', 'Bronze Ore' or 'Sword' never appears on the Snail.
- (b) Membership authoritative: entries == parsed HS lines (deduped across categories); removing an HS line in a test copy fails validation.
- (c) Every resolved chance re-parses from raw_value.
- (d) Meso amount authority is MeowDB for owner 2 and Hidden Street for 3/4/5/9; chance authority is KuroDB with 0.4; the Sentinel has none.
- (e) Unresolved rows stay in the table, have chance 0 and appear in DropRates.unresolved(owner) and in the validation report.
- (f) Every runtime-eligible item_id exists.
- (g) A never-join-by-id test: kuro_item_id 4000001 must map to 356, not 348.
- (h) Progression: 347/349/356/348/351 at 1.0; 441/442 at 1.0 with gate 1012.
Rewrite test_drops_roller.gd and test_drops_data.gd for the new policy:
- seeded determinism
- quest gating: 347 drops only with 1005 active, and 441/442 only with 1012 active
- unresolved rows never rolled
- the _obtainable helper passes active quests
Fix test_loot_visuals.gd:52 to iterate only runtime-eligible rows. New game/tests/unit/test_drops_simulation.gd, the large offline simulation:
- seeded; 200k kills for each monster plus the box
- asserts |observed - p| <= 4*sqrt(p(1-p)/n) for p >= 0.01
- a 2M-kill run for the 0.0008 rows (Red Snail and Orange Mushroom), tagged slow or run through a game/tools/drop_sim.gd report into _scratch
- checks meso bag rate against 0.4 and that amount bounds and range coverage are uniform
- the simulation never feeds back into data

implementation_plan.step: 8. Wooden Box runtime
implementation_plan.detail:
Pure rules:
- New game/scripts/core/breakables/breakable_rules.gd: hits_to_break from the canonical record (4); a landed basic attack counts 1 hit (labelled interpretation); per-placement respawn_s.
- MapInstanceState gains reactors[] {placement_index, hits, broken_until} in snapshot() and restore, ticking on the pausable game clock like mob slots.
Placement:
- Adapt the 19 canonical px placements into isometric positions with a placement sidecar, the same way spawn slots are adapted: game/data/misostory/breakable_placements.json, or a world sidecar emitted by the Blender exporter.
- Keep boxes clear of portals and NPCs.
Actor and system:
- New game/scripts/actors/breakables/breakable_system.gd and wooden_box.gd: a proxy crate model, a hit wobble and a break FX.
- attack_candidates() is merged into PlayerCombat's candidate list (player_combat.gd:203).
On break:
- DropRoller.roll('0000001', db, rng, {active_quests}), then Events.loot_dropped. LootSystem already handles the drops.
- No EXP and no mesos.
Debug commands: break_box and reactors.
implementation_plan.tests:
Unit test game/tests/unit/test_breakables.gd covers:
- 3 hits do not break a box and 4 do
- a broken box respawns after respawn_s (90/120/180 per placement)
- the box state survives a map change
- without quest 1012 a box drops at most an Apple (0.25)
- with 1012 active it drops 1 board and 1 screw
- it never drops mesos and never drops Egg
New real-game scenario game/tools/playtest/scenarios/test_h_breakable.gd: accept 1012, break 3 boxes, pick up the items with Z, complete 1012 with Pio.

implementation_plan.step: 9. Docs and decision log
implementation_plan.detail: Write docs/canonical/drops.md (or a section in monsters.md) with the policy, schema v2, crosswalk rules, id traps and the unresolved list. Update docs/runtime/ITEMS.md (l.21-35, 75-76), CONTENT_AUTHORING.md (how to add a drop or crosswalk row), DEFERRED.md (remove the l.23 placeholder line; list the unresolved drops and ambiguous rows; drop the breakables item once done) and tools/kurodb/captures/README.md:4 (membership is HS for monsters). Add an ITERATION_LOG entry for any new interpretation: meso range distribution, quest-gating semantics, and the 'any landed hit counts' box rule.

implementation_plan.step: 10. Re-measure in the real game, no re-tuning
implementation_plan.detail: Re-run bash scripts/playtest.sh for test_b_combat, test_c_progression, test_d_inventory and the new test_h_breakable. Expected shifts: one shell or cap per kill, mesos down 35-55%, almost no equipment drops. Where a scenario's budget fails (for example test_d_inventory '100 mesos needed' or loot assertions on now-excluded items like 541, 1195, 417), adjust the scenario's hunting plan or kill count. Never change canonical values. Record the before/after per-kill economics in the playthrough report.

defects.title: Natural HP regeneration still implements the Iteration Two placeholder, not the owner's rule
defects.detail: NaturalRecoveryRule.step (natural_recovery_rule.gd:58-67) zeroes the accumulated rest on any ineligible tick and at full HP. It also requires since_combat >= delay_s (5 s), and NaturalRecovery (natural_recovery.gd:32-38,74-81) treats monster hits, misses/guards and attack starts as combat (reset plus delay). Owner rule (ITERATION_THREE_BRIEF.md 'Resolve Iteration Two Placeholder', 'Natural HP Regeneration'): walking, jumping and attacking PAUSE the timer without resetting it, and there is no combat delay. Example from the brief: stand 6 s, move 5 s, stand 4 s must produce one tick. The current code produces none (it needs 10 continuous seconds after the move, and 15 s after any hit or attack). combat.json:60-67 also labels the numbers as a MisoStory adaptation (verified false), where they should be the owner's decision.

defects.title: Attacking is not modelled as a pause state; a planted ground attack looks like standing still
defects.detail: Once the 5 s delay is removed, nothing makes the player ineligible during an attack. AttackLockInput (attack_lock_input.gd) zeroes the move vector during a ground attack's lockout, so velocity is 0 and is_resting() returns true. The eligibility test must read PlayerCombat.is_attacking() (player_combat.gd:225) and any future skill-cast lockout.

defects.title: No sitting and no usable chair: the Green Relaxer is an inert inventory record
defects.detail: The X 'sit' action is bound but unread and hidden (controls.gd:20, controls_panel.gd:16). The player state machine has no seated state (player_controller.gd:47). The inventory window refuses Setup items (inventory_window.gd:160-178 NOT_USABLE), and quickslots accept only consumables (quickslots.gd:45). The brief's DoD requires 'Sitting permits natural HP regeneration', 'chairs work', and 'obtain and use a chair'. Quest 1012's canonical reward (522: setup.hp_recovery_bonus 30 every 10 s, stacking with natural regen per recovery.json chairs[0]) has no gameplay effect.

defects.title: No Beginner skill system: 9 canonical SP are earned but cannot be spent, and the 3 skills cannot be used
defects.detail: beginner.json holds complete per-level data for 0001000/0001001/0001002. CharacterState.skills is never written, there is no SP spending, no skill window (K reserved and hidden), no casting, no MP or shell costs, no cooldowns and no timed effects. The baseline test_c ends at level 8 with 7 unspent SP. Only CombatFormula.resolve_fixed_damage (combat_formula.gd:477-495) plus combat.json fixed_damage_skills exist. The DoD requires 'All applicable Beginner skills implemented', 'Skill behavior uses canonical data', and 'skills persist'.

defects.title: No timed-effect (buff/heal-over-time) or cooldown runtime
defects.detail: CharacterState.effects is persisted and StatCalculator.effect_bonuses (stat_calculator.gd:153-158) already feeds speed into PlayerController.refresh_stats. Nothing creates, ticks or expires effects, and consumables.gd:5-6 defers buffs to an 'effect system' that does not exist. Nimble Feet and Recovery depend on it.

defects.title: Regen accumulator is not saved; with a no-reset rule, quit/continue silently discards accumulated time
defects.detail: NaturalRecoveryRule.rest lives only on the runtime node. The brief's regen test list includes 'save/load', and the save-state audit lists skills, chairs and HP. A field (default 0) in CharacterState is needed, or a documented decision that load starts at 0.

defects.title: Docs point natural regeneration at a non-existent file
defects.detail: docs/canonical/README.md:74 says 'Natural HP/MP regeneration amount and interval' live in game/data/misostory/recovery.json, but that file does not exist (the values are in combat.json natural_recovery). docs/runtime/MONSTERS_AND_COMBAT_RUNTIME.md:333-350 describes the old rule.

defects.title: Stale playtest wording claims there is no natural HP regeneration
defects.detail: test_c_progression.gd:20 says '(no natural regeneration exists)'. Its soft check at :1100 is labelled 'the hunter never died (there is no natural HP regeneration)' and WARNs in the baseline report (24 deaths at levels 7-8 in 000001000). The 5 s combat delay plus reset means regen almost never fires while hunting; this text should be updated with the new rule. test_d_inventory.gd:198-206 also still describes regen as 'out of combat'.

defects.title: Regen ownership is coupled to MonsterSystem
defects.detail: NaturalRecovery is added to the player by MonsterSystem.attach_player (monster_system.gd:120-124). Sitting, chair bonuses and skill heal-over-time are player/character concerns. Putting regen, seat and effects on a player-side node (or the player scene) avoids a world without a MonsterSystem losing regen. This is not a bug today.

defects.title: Crouch / down-jump from Rain's quiz is not implemented
defects.detail: movement.json:62-65 records the quiz 1013 statement ('press the down arrow key, you can crouch, and then jump while crouching, to leap down to a lower platform'). PLAYER_AND_CAMERA.md:417 lists it as not implemented. It needs an explicit isometric adaptation decision or a documented exclusion in the parity manifest.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Record the owner's regen rule as data with its own provenance
implementation_plan.detail: Create game/data/misostory/recovery.json, matching the existing pointer in docs/canonical/README.md:74. Section natural_hp: {hp_per_tick 10, tick_s 10, timer "pause", eligible ["standing_still","sitting"], pauses ["walking","jumping","attacking"], never_exceeds_max_hp true}, with source {kind "project_owner_decision", date "2026-10-05", ref "docs/ITERATION_THREE_BRIEF.md#resolve-iteration-two-placeholder-natural-hp-regeneration"}. Also add chair_bonus_timing (see open questions) and recovery_skill_ticks (an adaptation for the Recovery tick gap, verified false). Add natural_mp {value null, status "unresolved_source_gap", reason quoting recovery.json gaps}. Remove natural_recovery from combat.json (delay_s and requires_standing_still disappear). Teach adaptation_checks.gd the new table and kind, and drop natural_recovery from the key list in test_combat_adaptations.gd:38. Update docs/canonical/README.md:74 and MONSTERS_AND_COMBAT_RUNTIME.md:333-350.
implementation_plan.tests: test_data_validation_adaptation.gd: a missing hp_per_tick or tick_s is an error, and natural_mp must stay null. test_combat_adaptations.gd updated.

implementation_plan.step: 2. Rewrite NaturalRecoveryRule as a pausing eligible-time clock
implementation_plan.detail: State: elapsed_s (eligible seconds toward the next tick). step(dt, eligible, hp, max_hp, extra_hp_per_tick = 0) -> heal. While eligible (and HP > 0), elapsed advances. While ineligible it is left untouched (pause). When elapsed >= tick_s: elapsed -= tick_s, heal = min(hp_per_tick + extra, max_hp - hp). Full-HP handling per the owner's answer (default proposal: full HP counts as a pause). Remove note_combat, since_combat and delay_s. Add to_dict/from_dict for persistence.
implementation_plan.tests: Rewrite test_natural_recovery.gd with the brief's list: 10.0 continuous s gives +10; 9.9 s gives 0; partial accumulation (6 s eligible + 5 s ineligible + 4 s eligible gives exactly one tick at the end); movement pause; jump pause; attack pause (each ineligible span keeps elapsed); resume after pause; sitting is eligible; full HP clamp (46/50 gives +4, 50/50 gives 0); HP 0 gives 0; chair extra +30 gives 40 per tick; to_dict/from_dict round trip mid-accumulation.

implementation_plan.step: 3. One player 'activity' query that regen and skills share
implementation_plan.detail: Add PlayerController.activity() (or a small PlayerActivity helper) returning flags: walking (move intent non-zero or horizontal move_velocity > STILL_SPEED, including pushing against a wall), airborne (state AIR: jump, fall, knockback), climbing, seated, attacking (PlayerCombat.is_attacking()), casting (skill lockout), hitstun, dead, warping (not MapSession.is_idle()). Rewrite NaturalRecovery.is_eligible() = alive and idle session and (seated or (grounded and not walking/airborne/climbing/attacking/casting/hitstun)). Drop the Events.player_damaged / player_missed_by / attack_started connections. Consider moving NaturalRecovery creation out of MonsterSystem.attach_player into the player scene or a player-side vitals node.
implementation_plan.tests: New test_natural_recovery_node.gd on player_test_world plus BotInput and a PlayerCombat stub: walking, jump, attack lockout and climbing pause; standing in a dialogue (input disabled) is eligible; warp pauses; a knockback (airborne) pauses.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Persist the regen clock
implementation_plan.detail: Add CharacterState.regen_elapsed_s (default 0.0, serialized). NaturalRecovery reads it and writes it back. No schema bump is needed because the field has a default (character_state.gd header rule). Document it in SAVES.md.
implementation_plan.tests: test_save_roundtrip.gd includes regen_elapsed_s. A v1 fixture without the field loads with 0.

implementation_plan.step: 5. Seated state in the player controller
implementation_plan.detail: Add sit(chair_id) / stand(reason) / is_seated(), signals sat_down/stood_up, and a SeatLockInput decorator (pattern of attack_lock_input.gd) or a State.SIT. You can sit only when grounded, alive, input enabled, not attacking, climbing or in hitstun, and the session is idle. While seated: no walking or jumping; a move or jump press stands up (the press is consumed); attack and skill presses are ignored (owner decision); interact and pickup per decision. Forced stand on apply_knockback, teleport (warps, respawn, fall recovery), die, and losing the chair item. PlayerVisual sit pose (presentation only). Seated state is never saved (load standing).
implementation_plan.tests: test_player_movement.gd: sit blocks walking; a jump press stands up without jumping; teleport, knockback and death stand up; you cannot sit airborne or on a ladder. test_player_combat: no attack while seated.

implementation_plan.step: 6. Chair use: inventory, X key, quickslot, +30 HP bonus

A ChairService/ItemService.use_chair(item_id) that toggles sit through the player. inventory_window.activate_slot: a Setup chair sits or stands (no longer NOT_USABLE). implementation_plan.step: 7. Rewrite the regen playtest for the pause rule
implementation_plan.detail: regen.gd: HP set low (api setup); 6 s still, 5 s walking, 4 s still gives one tick (pause, not reset); jump spam over 10 s gives none, and the earlier accumulation is kept; held attack gives none; sitting on 522 gives 40 per 10 s; full HP clamp; save at about 6 s accumulated, then Continue and stand 4 s gives a tick (if persisted). Fix the stale wording in test_c_progression.gd:20,1100 and test_d_inventory.gd:198-206.

implementation_plan.step: 8. Timed effects and cooldowns
implementation_plan.detail: An EffectBook (pure) over CharacterState.effects. Entries: {id, source "skill:<id>", kind buff|hot|cooldown, bonuses {speed: 10}, remaining_s, hp_total/ticks}. A player-side EffectTicker node advances remaining_s in game time, applies heal-over-time through Game.change_hp, and emits Events.stats_changed on add and expire (PlayerController.refresh_stats picks up the speed). Re-casting is blocked by the cooldown. The persistence policy (keep remaining time or drop on load) follows the owner's decision.
implementation_plan.tests: test_effects.gd: a speed +10 effect raises StatCalculator.speed by 10 (capped at 140) and expires on time; heal-over-time totals exactly hp_total over 30 s and never exceeds Max HP; save round-trips effects per the policy.

implementation_plan.step: 9. Skill data and rules (SkillDef / SkillBook)
implementation_plan.detail: SkillDef.from_canonical(db.formula("beginner").skills[i]) plus attack_speed three_snails and attack_styles three_snails_targeting. SkillBook (pure): learn(c, id) spends 1 SP, the level is capped at max_level 3, and Beginner skills have no prerequisites. can_cast(c, id, ctx) checks: learned; MP >= mp_cost; Three Snails' per-level shell (348/349/351, qty 1) present; cooldown free; cast position (Three Snails ground only; Recovery and Nimble Feet ground, air or rope); alive; not seated. cast() applies the costs through Game.change_mp and ItemService (item_lost so quest 1011's Blue Snail Shell count updates).
implementation_plan.tests: test_skill_book.gd: 9 SP max all three at 3; no 4th level; no SP refused; costs per level exactly as in beginner.json (MP 3/4/5 + shells, 5/10/15, 4/7/10); cooldowns 120/180; Three Snails refused in the air or on a rope; refused without a shell or MP.

implementation_plan.step: 10. Skill casting runtime (PlayerSkills)
implementation_plan.tests: test_player_skills.gd on monster_test_rig: a Snail at 200 px ahead is hit for exactly 15/25/40 (or misses on the hit roll); targets at 40 px, 320 px or behind are not hit; the vertical band holds; a shell and MP are consumed per cast; the lockout matches the timing; Nimble Feet changes walk speed; Recovery heals its total.

implementation_plan.detail: New scripts/ui/windows/skill_window.gd (MisoWindow): the three Beginner skills with icon or name, level/max, SP left, a '+' per skill (SkillBook.learn), description and per-level cost and effect from canonical data, and a 'bind to key' action using the inventory window's key picker. Register it in windows_root.gd ACTIONS 'toggle_skills' and remove it from controls_panel NOT_AVAILABLE. Quickslot values become typed ("skill:<id>" string prefix, which avoids a migration, or {kind,id} with a v1->v2 SaveMigrations step and fixture). The HUD quickslot bar shows skill cooldowns.

open_questions: Regen at full HP: should the eligible-time clock hold (pause) while HP is full, or keep running? The brief only forbids resetting. Proposal: treat full HP as a pause.

Is being touched or knocked back while standing still a pause? Under the rule as written, only walking, jumping and attacking pause; a knockback pauses only because the player is airborne. Confirm that the 5 s out-of-combat delay is removed entirely.
Is hanging motionless on a ladder or rope eligible? It is neither standing nor sitting. Proposal: not eligible (pause).
Should the accumulated regen time persist across save/load and quit, or restart at 0 on load? Proposal: persist it in CharacterState.regen_elapsed_s.

Chair bonus timing: does the +30 HP share the natural 10 s eligible clock (40 HP per tick while seated on 522), or run on its own seated-only 10 s clock? MeowDB says only 'additional 30 HP every 10 seconds'.

What does X do with no chair? MeowDB documents no ground sit and no map seat placements. Options: a notice 'no chair', sit on the last-used chair, or a ground-sit adaptation. Is a ground sit (no chair) 'sitting' for the owner's rule?
While seated: does attack, skill, NPC talk or pickup stand the player up, or is it ignored? Do potions work while seated? (MeowDB is silent.)

Natural MP recovery: MeowDB is silent. Keep none (current) as an explicit unresolved gap, or does the owner want to supply a rule? Three Snails, Recovery and Nimble Feet all cost MP, and a Lv1 Beginner has 5 MP.

summary:
The Iteration Two save system is sound. It uses a versioned JSON envelope (save_version 1) with atomic writes through .tmp, read back and rename. It keeps one .bak generation, recovers a slot whose save file is missing from that backup, and has a SaveMigrations registry with a v0->v1 step. Autosave is debounced and gated by can_save(). Character identity, gender, level/EXP, HP/MP, AP/base stats, SP (as a number), mesos, inventory (including the Setup tab), equipment, item quickslots, quest status/kill/use/talk progress, quest completion, current map (entry + resume) and respawn reference are all persisted. Each has unit or real-game evidence (test_save_roundtrip, test_quest_save_load, and the baseline playtests test_d_inventory #57-77, test_c_progression #25, test_e_quest #80 and test_f_death D1/D2).

Gaps against Phase 14 and the Definition of Done:
1. Random quest rewards already received are not recorded. QuestEngine.complete has rolled.random_picks in hand (quest_engine.gd:409/456), but QuestLog.complete stores only status, completed_at and completions (quest_log.gd:122-126). A real Iteration Two save (test_e_quest/slot1) has 1008 completed and the Green Headband (713) in the bag, with no record of it.
2. QuestLog.from_dict rebuilds each entry from a fixed 5-key template and whitelists the progress keys (quest_log.gd:192-250). Any quest-state key Iteration Three adds would be silently dropped on load. CharacterState top-level fields are forward compatible; QuestLog is not.
3. Nothing persists the skill system's state beyond the bare skills/sp fields. Effects and cooldowns would be keyed to Game.clock, which restarts at 0 every process. The round-trip fixture already pins an absolute "until": 512.25.
4. Quickslots hold bare item ids and only consumables can be bound, so skills and chairs cannot be bound.
5. The natural-regen accumulator lives on the NaturalRecovery node, is not persisted, and is not restored or reset on character_replaced.
6. resume.map_content_hash is written but never compared on load. Iteration Three's Blender trap fixes could resume an Iteration Two save inside changed geometry (F1-9 precedent).
7. There is no orphan-item handling. Iteration Three's Hidden Street membership removes the ores 321/413/415/417 and 1195/651/710 as Maple Island drops, and test_c_progression's save holds all four ores.
8. There is no real Iteration Two save fixture under game/tests/data. Migration is tested only with a synthetic v0 object.
9. There is no pre-migration copy of the file.

The proposal is schema v2, with a single SaveMigrations step v1->v2 that does four things: types the quickslot values, marks completed quest entries rewards_received {recorded:false}, sets quests.format to 2, and clears effects (every Iteration Two save has effects: []). Additive fields (natural_recovery.hp_rest_s, cooldowns) are added with defaults. Fixture tests use 5 real Iteration Two saves promoted from _scratch/it3/baseline_playtests.

Seated state, breakable state, monster/drop state, Game.clock and RNG stay unpersisted by design, each with a 'stands up / respawns on load' test. Nothing blocks loading Iteration Two saves today. No canonical values live in this domain: respawn_reference is recomputed from the canonical return_map_id, so there are no canonical mismatches.

defects.title: Random quest rewards already received are never recorded
defects.detail: QuestEngine.complete rolls the random/selection picks (quest_engine.gd:409) and returns them (:456), but persists only QuestLog.complete(quest_id, now()) (:447 -> quest_log.gd:122-126: status, completed_at, completions). Phase 14 and the Definition of Done item 'random reward state persists' cannot be met. Real It2 evidence: _scratch/it3/baseline_playtests/test_e_quest/saves/slot1.json has 1008 completed and 713 Green Headband in the equip tab, with no record of which of the 7 canonical hats was rolled. The pick must not be inferred from inventory later, because 713 is also a Hidden Street Orange Mushroom drop (Red Headband is) and items can be sold.

defects.title: QuestLog.from_dict silently drops any quest-entry or progress key Iteration Three adds
defects.detail: from_dict rebuilds each entry from a fixed template {status, progress, started_at, completed_at, completions} (quest_log.gd:205-211). _clean_progress whitelists kills/used/talked/visited/other (:234-250). A new key (rewards_received, quiz attempts, breakable interactions) round-trips in memory but is lost on load. SAVES.md:214 ('a field added with a default needs no migration') holds for CharacterState top-level fields only, not for the quest blob. The existing round-trip test would not catch it unless _rich_character populates the new key.

defects.title: resume.map_content_hash is written but never checked; It3 geometry fixes can resume It2 saves inside changed terrain
defects.detail: MapSession.capture_location writes resume.map_content_hash = def.content_hash (map_session.gd:487-488). ArrivalResolver.resolve_load (arrival_resolver.gd:57-69) accepts any resume that passes the physical validate_resume (island_world.gd:649-665: in-region, grounded, capsule clear, not in a portal trigger). F1-9 (ITERATION_LOG.md:229) shows autosave+Continue resuming a player inside a pocket. Iteration Three's Phase 13 stuck-region fixes change collision, so It2 resume points in edited maps are unvetted. A hash mismatch should demote resume to entry.

defects.title: No handling of saved item ids that the Iteration Three item set no longer defines
defects.detail: SaveDocument.decode (save_document.gd:99), Inventory.from_dict (inventory.gd:137-170), Equipment.from_dict (equipment.gd:62-74) and quickslot reads never consult the db for item ids. Under the Hidden Street drop membership (tools/hiddenstreet/captures/monsters.json: 'Ore drop: -' for all 6 monsters; no Ice Jeans, Metal Wand or Red Skullcap), the It2 drop-only items 321/413/415/417 (ores), 1195, 651 and 710 lose their Maple Island source. The real It2 save test_c_progression/saves/slot1.json holds 321, 413, 415 and 417. 933/934/938/939/1157/1305/1306 stay reachable via Pan's shop. If the items domain prunes those definitions, loaded saves carry dangling ids. Equipment bonuses silently become {} and UI/sell paths are unverified.

defects.title: Natural-regen accumulator is node state, not persisted and not restored or reset on character replacement
defects.detail: NaturalRecoveryRule.rest/since_combat (natural_recovery_rule.gd:20-23) live in the NaturalRecovery node (natural_recovery.gd:12). Nothing reads or writes the character on Game.character_replaced. Under the It2 reset rule the load warp zeroes it implicitly (is_resting false while MapSession is not idle). Under the It3 pause rule a stale accumulator would carry into a newly loaded character or slot. The brief's regen test list includes 'save/load'.

defects.title: Timed state uses the per-process Game.clock, which is not persisted
defects.detail: Game.clock (game_state.gd:34) restarts at 0 every process and is not saved. The round-trip fixture pins an absolute expiry 'until': 512.25 in effects (test_save_roundtrip.gd:128), the pattern Nimble Feet/Recovery buffs and skill cooldowns would copy. After a quit-reload they would last the wrong time. Quest started_at/completed_at are also session-clock values (informational only today).

defects.title: Quickslots cannot represent skill or chair bindings
defects.detail: CharacterState.quickslots is key -> item id String. MisoQuickslots.can_bind admits consumables only (quickslots.gd:45-48), and to_dict/from_dict use a shallow duplicate (character_state.gd:81, :112). The brief's Skill UI asks for 'keyboard binding or practical activation'. Typed values need a migration and a deep copy.

defects.title: No real Iteration Two save fixture; migration tested only with a synthetic v0 dict
defects.detail: game/tests/data holds only parity_vectors.json. test_save_migrations.gd:48-72 builds a v0 object in code. Real v1 saves produced by this build exist only in git-ignored _scratch/it3/baseline_playtests/*/saves/slot*.json (12 files), so 'save migration works' (Definition of Done) has no regression anchor.

defects.title: No durable pre-migration copy
defects.detail: SaveStore keeps one .bak generation (save_store.gd:95-101). After loading a migrated v1 save, the first save puts v1 into .bak and the second save overwrites it. A faulty v1->v2 step would destroy the only copy of a player's Iteration Two progress.

defects.title: Module version fields are written but never read
defects.detail: inventory.version (inventory.gd:14,131), equipment.version (equipment.gd:15,59) and quests.format (quest_log.gd:28,187; comment says 'Bump with a migration in from_dict') are never checked by their from_dict. That leaves two versioning layers that can drift. Structural changes should live in SaveMigrations steps, which stamp the module fields.

defects.title: Inventory.from_dict trusts the saved tab and capacity
defects.detail: Items are restored into the tab named in the file without comparing to the canonical inventory_tab (inventory.gd:144-170). A canonical tab correction would leave old items misplaced. The known memory-exhaustion risk from a huge saved capacity or index is still open (SAVES.md:130-132).

Add an optional entry key rewards_received {recorded: bool, random: [{item_id, count}], selection: {item_id, count} or {}}, and add QuestLog.record_rewards(quest_id, random_picks, selection_pick). from_dict keeps rewards_received through a cleaner that normalizes ids to String and counts to int. Also keep any unknown entry keys verbatim and preserve unknown progress keys from _clean_progress, so a later addition is never silently dropped. In QuestEngine.complete, call quest_log().record_rewards(quest_id, rolled.random_picks, rolled.selection_pick) right after quest_log().complete(...) (quest_engine.gd:447), recording {recorded: true} even when both are empty. On forfeit and re-accept of a repeatable quest, keep the last completion's record.

Same for 1011 (559 or 558). test_quest_log (unit): unknown entry and progress keys survive from_dict.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Decide and implement quickslot value typing

Update MisoQuickslots item_for/bind/unbind/move, add skill_for/bind_skill, and allow Setup chair items in can_bind if the chair UX uses a key. Update the HUD quickslot bar and inventory/equipment window drag paths. Change CharacterState.quickslots copies to duplicate(true). The alternative (a separate skill_keys dict) needs no migration but needs cross-dict conflict handling in the UI. The choice is an open question.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Add the additive CharacterState fields for It3 mechanics
implementation_plan.detail: Add natural_recovery: {hp_rest_s: float, since_combat_s: float}, default {}. cooldowns: {skill_id: remaining_s float}, default {}. The effects entry contract becomes {id, remaining_s, ...}, never an absolute Game.clock time. NaturalRecovery reads and writes the accumulator from Game.character, so it is restored on load and naturally per-character, clamped to [0, tick_s). The skill system decrements cooldowns and effects by unpaused delta. Seated state, breakable state, Game.clock and RNG stay unpersisted. The sitting system clears seated on Game.character_replaced and map transitions. Update test_save_roundtrip _rich_character: replace effects 'until': 512.25 with remaining_s and add the new fields.

New unit test: 6 s eligible, save/decode, 4 s eligible -> exactly one 10 HP tick (pause semantics across save). character_replaced to another character uses that character's accumulator, not the previous one.

implementation_plan.step: 5. SaveMigrations v1 -> v2 step and CURRENT_VERSION = 2
implementation_plan.detail: Register 1 -> '_v1_to_v2' (name 'v1_quest_rewards_typed_quickslots') in _init; never edit _v0_to_v1. The step changes the following and leaves location, world and inventory untouched; it returns {} if the character is not a Dictionary. (a) Every quests.quests entry with status 'completed' and no rewards_received gets {recorded: false}. This needs no db lookup and is honest: v1 recorded no reward for any quest. (b) quests.format becomes 2. (c) Each quickslots String value becomes {kind:'item', id: value}; non-string values are dropped. (d) effects become []: v1 had no effect producer, and all 12 baseline saves hold []. (e) Absent natural_recovery and cooldowns are left for from_dict defaults. inventory.version and equipment.version stay 1 because their format is unchanged. With step 3's alternative (no typed quickslots), the bump is still required for (a) and (b).

implementation_plan.step: 6. Load-time content checks for saved item ids (lossless)
implementation_plan.detail: With a db, SaveDocument.decode appends a warning for every item id in inventory, equipment and quickslots that db.has('items', id) rejects, and for any inventory entry whose tab differs from the canonical inventory_tab. Items are kept, never deleted silently. The UI shows unknown items with a fallback icon and allows discard. Coordinate with the items/drops auditors: do not prune canonical item records It2 could have granted (at minimum 321/413/415/417/1195/651/710 plus everything in the It2 drop/shop/quest closure). Otherwise an It2 save loads with dangling ids.

implementation_plan.step: 7. Guard resume points with map_content_hash
implementation_plan.detail: In ArrivalResolver.resolve_load, if resume.map_content_hash is present and differs from defs.get_def(map_id).content_hash, skip the resume step: append an error/warning and use entry. implementation_plan.step: 8. Keep a one-time pre-migration copy
implementation_plan.detail: SaveService remembers migrations_applied/version_found of the last load per slot. On the first save_game after loading a migrated file, if '<slot>.json.pre-v<found>' does not exist, SaveStore copies the current main file there before writing. SaveStore.delete removes it too. list_slots already ignores it, because the name does not end in .json or .json.bak.

summary:
Most of the Phase 12 world feedback is already built and tested. Interact prompts, portal cues with destination names, pickup notices for items and mesos, quest markers over NPCs, damage numbers and HP bars, the level-up flourish, the AP badge, and the inventory-full and insufficient-mesos warnings are all wired to the canonical services (test_interaction_*, test_loot_system, test_ui_hud, test_shop_ui_window, test_monster_fx, test_interaction_main_flow). What is missing or partial:

1. No minimap. M is reserved in controls.gd:26 and hidden by ControlsPanel.NOT_AVAILABLE (controls_panel.gd:16). This fails the UI item in the Definition of Done.
2. No skills window. K is reserved, and quickslots take consumables only.
3. SP is granted at levels 2-10 (progression.gd:97) but shown only by the debug `char` command (debug_report.gd:203).
4. The quest log has no chain progression and no NPC location. The canonical quest_line, prerequisites and start_maps/end_maps fields exist, but QuestDef parses only followups.
5. Chairs in the Setup tab cannot be used from the inventory (inventory_window.gd:173-178 returns NOT_USABLE). X (sit) is reserved.
6. Shops are indicated only by the name-tag function title and the portal prompt's destination name.
7. The map name shows only in the arrival banner, which fades. The map id is shown only in debug mode.

Only debug tools show: the map id, a map's full portal layout (the `portals` command and draw layer), SP, NPC positions off-screen, and the hidden portal 000001020 in00.

Minimap data:
- The canonical minimap block is 2D only: size and centre in px with has_image, and 0x0 for 000000061, 000001011 and 000001013. Its image is Nexon art, so it is unusable.
- Every input for an isometric minimap is already in the runtime. Each MapDefinition has a footprint (all 25 are rotated rectangles, plus region_extensions), frame, base_y and y range. It also has 47 canonical PortalDefs (46 visible plus the hidden type-1 000001020 in00) with anchor_ground, inward, hidden and destination, and 21 NpcPlacements, all matching MeowDB one for one.
- The sidecar adds routes, climbables, spawn_regions, prop_instances and one shared gameplay-camera xform for all maps (right (0.707,0,0.707), up (0.455,0.766,-0.455), pitch 40 degrees).
- IslandWorld.collision_root holds each chunk's Ground* trimesh (88 to 30,691 triangles per map). Bodies carry meta "chunk" equal to the slug; faces must be transformed by CollisionShape3D.global_transform.

Proposed design:
- Project world points with the gameplay camera basis: u = p dot right, v = -(p dot up). The minimap is then a scaled-down orthographic view matching what the player sees.
- Ground triangles are drawn tinted by height tier, with the footprint and routes as a fallback. Overlaid on them: visible canonical portals (swirl or door glyph, outward arrow, destination name, a shop badge when the destination hosts a shopkeeper), NPC dots with their quest-marker state and a shop or transport icon, the player arrow, and trail stubs.
- A title strip shows street and map name, plus the map id when Debug.overlay_enabled is on.
- It lives in a new ui_root subsystem scene, scenes/ui/minimap.tscn, with pure MinimapProjection and MinimapModel classes behind it.

defects.title: No minimap on any of the 25 maps
defects.detail: Definition of Done UI item 'Functional minimap exists for all playable maps' and brief Phase 11. toggle_minimap (M) is bound (controls.gd:26) but no script handles it. test_shell_screens.gd:132-140 enforces this through ControlsPanel.NOT_AVAILABLE. Playtests note that no exit is in view at any first arrival (DEFERRED.md:57, PLAYTHROUGH_REPORT.md:100). Today a map's exit layout is visible only through the debug `portals` command or draw layer.

defects.title: No skill window or skill quickslot binding (if Beginner skills are in scope)
defects.detail: Canonical beginner.json lists Three Snails 0001000, Recovery 0001001 and Nimble Feet 0001002, each max level 3. The brief's 'Skill UI' section asks for a window, levels, allocation, binding and persistence. K is reserved (controls.gd:25). Quickslots accept consumables only (MisoQuickslots; UI.md 'Known gaps'). Blocker status depends on the skills auditor confirming these skills apply during Maple Island.

defects.title: SP is granted but never shown to the player
defects.detail: Progression grants 1 SP per level-up at levels 2-10 (progression.gd:97,108-122; canonical beginner.json sp). No HUD element, window or log line shows it. Only the debug `char` command prints it (debug_report.gd:203). The brief requires normal play without developer tools.

defects.title: Quest log lacks chain progression and NPC location
defects.detail: The brief's 'Quest Log' section asks for the relevant NPC and chain progression. quest_window.gd shows start and turn-in NPC names only, and nothing about chains. The canonical data has quest_line.steps, prerequisites.quests, followup_quests and start_maps/end_maps for all 20 quests. QuestDef parses only followup_quests (quest_def.gd:63,164), and start_maps/end_maps are read only by validation (reference_checks.gd:555). Rain's 7-step quiz chain (1013-1019) and Sam -> Mai (1006 -> 1009 -> 1010) do not read as chains.

defects.title: Chairs cannot be used from the inventory; no sit handling
defects.detail: inventory_window.gd:173-178 sends every item that is neither equipment nor a consumable to ItemCodes.NOT_USABLE, so a Setup-tab chair (The Green Relaxer, the brief's Phase 9) cannot be used. sit (X) is reserved and unhandled (controls.gd:20, controls_panel.gd:16). The UI side depends on the chairs/sitting service.

defects.title: Players see 'Tutorial Jr. Sentinel (placeholder)'
defects.detail: monster_visual.gd:483-490 attaches a Label3D reading '<name> (placeholder)' to any monster without a proxy, and test_monster_fx.gd:68 asserts it. Its HP bar also crosses the tag (DEFERRED.md). Belongs to the monsters/art domain. The UI concern is that placeholder wording reaches the player.

defects.title: Shops are hard to discover from outside
defects.detail: Pan, Sid and Lucy stand inside interiors (000000061, 000001011, 000001013). Their function title appears on the name tag only once the player is inside. From Southperry or Amherst the only hint is the door prompt naming the store. Add a minimap shop badge on doors whose destination hosts a Shopkeeper.

defects.title: Map name is transient; the map id appears only in the debug overlay
defects.detail: MisoMapBanner shows the street and name for about 3.85 s on arrival (map_banner.gd:11-13), then nothing. The brief wants the canonical map name on the minimap and the canonical map id in debug mode.

defects.title: Quest markers cover only on-screen, current-map NPCs, and level-locked quests show nothing
defects.detail: NpcPresenter draws markers in screen space only for visible current-map NPCs. Quests below the player's level (1007 min 2; 1009 and 1011 min 3; 1012-1019 min 5) produce no marker and no quest-log entry until the level is reached. Classic behaviour is similar, but the minimap should repeat the marker state for NPCs out of view.

implementation_plan.step: 1. World API: ground faces per map
implementation_plan.detail: Add IslandWorld.ground_faces(map_id) -> PackedVector3Array (cached per map id). Look up def.slug from defs. Walk collision_root.find_children('*', 'StaticBody3D'), keeping bodies with get_meta('chunk') == slug and a name starting with 'Ground' (_place_chunk, island_world.gd:259-297). For each CollisionShape3D child holding a ConcavePolygonShape3D, take shape.get_faces() and apply CollisionShape3D.global_transform: get_faces() is shape-local. Optionally add wall_faces(map_id) the same way, from non-Ground bodies of that chunk. Do not walk the visual glbs.
implementation_plan.tests: New test in a world test file, world-only: SKIP without INCLUDE_WORLD, following test_map_camera_bounds.gd:10-23. For all 25 maps: faces non-empty and divisible by 3; at least 90% of the face centroids in XZ inside def.footprint (or its AABB plus 2 m); y within [def.y_min, def.y_max].

implementation_plan.step: 2. Pure projection: MinimapProjection
implementation_plan.detail: New game/scripts/ui/minimap/minimap_projection.gd (class MinimapProjection, RefCounted). from_basis(basis) reuses CameraMath.basis_from_xform_array on def.sidecar.cameras.gameplay.xform. Every map shares right (0.70711,0,0.70711) and up (0.455,0.766,-0.455), but read it from data rather than code. project(p: Vector3) -> Vector2(p.dot(basis.x), -p.dot(basis.y)): the gameplay camera's own orthographic projection, so on-screen up (W, camera forward) is up on the minimap and raised tiers sit higher, as in the game view. fit(points, widget_size, margin) -> Transform2D: uniform scale, centred. unproject is not needed. clamp_to_rect(pt, rect) -> {pos, clamped, angle} handles a player off the footprint on a trail.
implementation_plan.tests: New default-suite test game/tests/unit/test_ui_minimap_projection.gd (no world needed): (a) for a Camera3D with that basis and PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL, project() differs from camera.unproject_position() only by one uniform scale and offset (sample 20 points); (b) moving the input along the camera ground-forward axis decreases y; (c) fit keeps the aspect ratio and puts every input point inside widget_size minus margin; (d) clamp_to_rect keeps the direction.

implementation_plan.step: 3. Pure model: MinimapModel
implementation_plan.detail:
New game/scripts/ui/minimap/minimap_model.gd. MinimapModel.build(def: MapDefinition, defs: MapDefinitions, db: ContentDB, ground_faces := PackedVector3Array()) returns {map_id, name, street (canonical maps/<id>.json), outline (def.footprint_layout plus def.region_extensions ring lines), ground (projected triangles with a tier index from (y - base_y) bucketed to about 1.5 m), climbables (sidecar.climbables bottom/top), routes (sidecar.routes polylines: the fallback when ground_faces is empty, e.g. headless or 000000021 with 88 triangles), portals, npcs, trails}.
- portals: one per PortalDef with is_canonical() and not hidden, giving {id, pos: anchor_ground, out_dir: -inward, kind: portal_type edge|door, dest_map_id, dest_name, dest_shop: any NPC on the destination map whose canonical record has a non-null shop}. Arrival gates (TYPE_ARRIVAL) are excluded. How to treat the hidden portal is an open question.
- npcs: {npc_id, name, pos from NpcPlacement.transform.origin, roles from npcs/<id>.json (Shopkeeper/Transport/Quest Giver), shop_id}.
- trails: defs.trails_of(map_id) centre polylines with other_map(map_id).
Cache by map id plus content_hash.
implementation_plan.tests: New game/tests/unit/test_ui_minimap_model.gd. It needs WorldSidecars, so it prints SKIP without INCLUDE_WORLD, like test_map_camera_bounds.gd; the projection test in step 2 stays in the default suite. For all 25 maps: name and street equal canonical; portal ids equal canonical type-2 portals (46 in total; 000001020 in00 handled per the chosen policy) and destination names equal canonical to_map_name; npc ids equal canonical npcs (21 in total); dest_shop is true exactly for 000000060.in00, 000001010.in00 and 000001010.in02; Shopkeeper NPCs are 16, 20 and 21, Transport is 15; arrival gates never appear; interiors 000000061, 000001011 and 000001013 build a model even though their canonical minimap is 0x0.

summary:
The traversal checks that exist work. On 2026-10-04 the route sweep made 360 route runs with 0 failures and 87 link runs with 0 failures. The baseline test_a_traversal on 2026-10-05 visited 25/25 maps and used 47/47 portals on foot, with 477 checks and 0 failures. world_checks presses Up at every portal and checks the arrival. But the systematic stuck-region scan (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.13, the L1 flood fill) was never built (MAP_ARCHITECTURE.md:713 and :849, DEFERRED.md). The only guard against traps is trap_probe, which tests 2 known spots and has a weak pass rule.

To answer "how would a scanner work and what does it cost", I built a scratch prototype in an isolated copy. It is not committed: _scratch/godot_runs/audit_traversal/game/_audit/bench.gd. It builds the island collision through IslandWorld.build_now (1.0 s). It samples surfaces the feet can stand on in a 0.35 m grid, using the controller's own rules: ground layers walkable, blocking and scenery, floor angle at most 38 degrees, and the body capsule (r 0.3, from 0.45 to 1.5 m above the feet) clear. An upward ray that also sees back faces rejects surfaces buried inside solid geometry. It builds directed edges for walking, drops, conservative jumps and ladders, then does forward reachability from the entry points and backward reachability from the exits. The whole run covers all 25 maps in 81 s wall: 1.43 M nodes, 10.7 M edges, 3.6 M rays and 12.9 M capsule queries. A ray costs 2.7-4.0 us and a capsule query 1.0-1.4 us.

The prototype found a new, systematic trap class: slots at map corners. A player who walks off the terrain edge at a map corner drops 2.3-2.6 m into a slot between the rounded plinth top and the square containment ring, onto the map's own Ground.
- **Confirmed in the real game with real input:** 000000041 (Snail Hunting Ground II) at local (64.70, -2.32, 0.17). trap_probe FAILs it: best escape 0.70 m, best rise 0.07 m.
- **Same class, wrongly passed:** 000001010 (Amherst) at local (76.70, -2.50, -37.57). trap_probe PASSes it, but every attempt ended 2.25-3.37 m below the map's level. This one result shows both a trap and a flaw in trap_probe's pass rule.
- **Confirmed with the real PlayerController on the island collision:** four more spots in 000001000, 000000041, 000001010 and 000001012. Each drops 2.3-2.6 m. The spot is inside the map's region, the floor is walkable and kill_y is below it, so fall recovery never fires. These are the same conditions under which the two Iteration Two traps resumed on Continue; save and Continue was not run here.

The probable root cause, from reading the code, is src/misostory/world.py:151-166. Map edges that carry a portal get only a 0.8 m plinth margin, and the plinth corners are rounded with radius 6.4 m, while the ring stands at footprint + 1.0 m with square corners. The hill skirt top sits at top - 2.25 m and the plinth bottom at top - 2.6 m; the measured drops (2.32-2.60 m) fall in that range. These traps break the Definition of Done item "No known unintended player trap remains".

The prototype also flagged large groups in 000000020, 000001004 and 000000061. The real controller then escaped from all three, so they are false positives. They expose three gaps in the prototype: jump edges only to the adjacent cell, ladders attached only within 0.9 m of their ends, and exits only at portal anchors. A production scanner needs multi-cell jump edges and a verification step that runs the real controller.

On the harness side, the driver API is solid: real input, walking on routes and the grid, trails, portals, combat, pickup, talk/choose, shop, save/reload and phases. But the composite play helpers are copied between scenarios and are not in the driver: _travel/_bfs, _converse, _use_by_double_click, _step_onto, _allocate, _drink and _respawn. There are no helpers for quizzes, breakables, sitting, chairs or skills. Walking ignores monsters: in the baseline Test A the walker died in 000001000 on legs 22 and 32. Cheat accounting only counts console() and api fallbacks. Real-game coverage of quests is 1002, 1006, 1007 and 1008 only. There is no every-quest scenario set and no clean end-to-end playthrough.

defects.title: Corner-slot traps at map edges (6 spots, 4 maps). One confirmed in main.tscn with real input, a second shown in main.tscn despite trap_probe's PASS, four with the real PlayerController
defects.detail:
A player who walks off the terrain edge at a map corner drops 2.3-2.6 m into the band between the plinth top and the containment ring (footprint + 1.0 m) and lands on the map's own Ground (layer 1). Jumping in 8 directions for 4 s each never rises more than 0.35 m, against the 1.35 m maximum reach. The spot is inside the map's region and above kill_y, so FallRecovery never fires and SafeGround records there. These are the same conditions under which the two Iteration Two traps resumed on Continue; save and Continue was not run here.

Evidence tiers:
- **Tier 1, main.tscn with real input (trap_probe):**
  - 000000041 local (64.70,-2.32,0.17): FAIL, best escape 0.70 m, rise 0.07 m (_scratch/it3/audit_traversal/trap_41_se/report.md).
  - 000001010 local (76.70,-2.50,-37.57): PASS (5.28 m flat), but every try ended 2.25-3.37 m below the map's level (_scratch/it3/audit_traversal/trap_1010_ne/report.md).
- **Tier 2, the real PlayerController on the island collision in PlayerTestWorld (scratch prototype):**
  - 000001000 (80.70,-2.60,-2.22), drop 2.60 m, kill_y -1.79
  - 000000041 (-0.70,-2.54,-44.70)
  - 000001010 (-0.57,-2.43,0.70)
  - 000001012 (24.70,-2.48,0.63)

Blender-local xy = (x, -z).

Probable root cause, from reading the code, so inspect one corner in Blender before editing: src/misostory/world.py:158-166. Edges that carry a portal get a thin 0.8 m plinth margin, and the corner radius is corner + min(margins) x 0.5 = 6.4 m. Meanwhile ContainmentBuilder stands the ring at footprint + 1.0 m with square convex corners (containment_builder.gd:5-10, 97-127). The hill skirt top is at bottom0 + 0.35 = top - 2.25 m and the plinth bottom at top - 2.6 m. The measured drops (2.32-2.60 m) fall exactly in that range. Every confirmed spot is at a corner next to a portal side. Not guarded today: test_world_static checks that rings are closed, not how deep the band behind them is.

defects.title: trap_probe's pass rule (ESCAPE_M = 4.0 m flat distance, or a 1.0 m rise) gives false PASSes
defects.detail: trap_probe.gd:10 and :79-80 count a spot as escaped when any try moves the body more than 4 m horizontally. A slot or pocket longer than 4 m passes even if the player never gets back to the main ground. Shown on 000001010 local (76.70,-2.50,-37.57): PASS with best escape 5.28 m, while the best rise was 0.25 m and every try stayed 2.25-3.37 m below the map's level. The second Iteration Two trap scored 3.95 m, just under the threshold (ITERATION_LOG F1-9). Fix the rule before adding the new spots to KNOWN_TRAPS, or the regression guard checks nothing.

implementation_plan.step: 1. Build StuckScan, the directed walkability-graph scanner, as a Godot tool
implementation_plan.detail:
Promote the scratch prototype into game/tools/stuck_scan.gd (class StuckScan, RefCounted) plus game/tools/stuck_scan_tool.gd and .tscn. Copy the CLI pattern of traversal_bot_tool.gd: --map, --cell (default 0.35), --verify, --out; default output docs/runtime/stuck_report.json, plus optional top-down PNG heat maps per map in _scratch for inspection, written with Image.save_png.

**Why Godot and not Blender:**
- The containment rings, plugs, trail walls and region extensions are built at runtime by ContainmentBuilder from sidecars and data/misostory.
- Layer classes and double_sided_trimesh are decided by IslandWorld._place_chunk.
- The feet stand on blocking and scenery tops (PLAYER_MASK, angle-only _is_floor).
- Only Godot can run the real PlayerController for verification.

**Collision data:** IslandWorld.build_now(db) with load_visuals=false, build_on_ready=false and attach_to_session=false (about 1.0 s). Jolt answers queries before the first physics step, the same as test_world_static.gd.

**Nodes:** every column of a 0.35 m grid over each map footprint (+1 m, with region extensions) and over each trail zone gets repeated downward rays on WALKABLE|BLOCKING|SCENERY, recording every surface top-down. A surface is standable when all three hold:
- its normal is within 38 degrees;
- the body capsule (r 0.3, from feet + 0.45 to feet + 1.5) is clear of PLAYER_MASK;
- it is not buried inside a closed solid: an upward ray with hit_back_faces must not hit a back face first.

Tag each node with its map/trail through RegionIndex.region_of and with its floor kind (walkable, prop top, scenery).

**Edges (read the numbers from MovementModel/movement.json; never hard-code them):**
- Walk: 8 neighbours, the FIRST surface at or below feet + step_up 0.45 in the neighbour column, |dy| <= 0.45, capsule clear at the midpoint.
- Drop: the first surface below in the neighbour column. If it is steep or not standable, flag 'landing to simulate'. If the column has no surface at all, flag 'fall-out' (kill_y is a failsafe, never counted as an exit).
- Jump-up: from 1 to 4 cells away, conservative reach J = jump_apex at Jump 100 + step_up - 0.2 = 1.15 m. Check with a capsule cast_motion along a sampled parabola (vertical speed 6.49 m/s, g 23.4, horizontal speed up to 3 m/s).
- Gap jump: up to 1.2 m horizontal, rise of 0.45 m or less, same arc sweep.
- Ladders/ropes from sidecar climbables: foot to top_exit unless descend_only, top_exit to foot; attach every node within grab radius 0.8 m and the grabbable height band (player_controller.gd:801-822), not just the end nearest the endpoint. Skip mid-air rope grabs (they could only cause false positives).
- No crouch drop-through: the controller does not have it.

**Entries:** player_spawns[], portal spawn_transforms, the arrival gate, respawn points.

**Exits:** press-Up portal triggers (including the type-1 hidden 000001020.in00), gate planes of edge-mode trails, doors.

**Result:** trapped = forward-reachable and not backward-reachable. Group the trapped nodes into components. For each component report:
- map-local and Blender-local (x, -z) coordinates and the height span;
- the in-edges that lead into it;
- what the floor is.

**Byproduct:** the reachability of every NPC talk zone, spawn slot, portal and Wooden Box placement from the entries.

**Cost:** the prototype measured 81 s wall for 25 maps (1.43 M nodes, 10.7 M edges, 3.6 M rays at 2.7-4 us, 12.9 M capsule queries at 1.0-1.4 us). With arc sweeps expect 2-5 minutes; a 0.25 m grid roughly doubles that. Development time: about 1 day.

implementation_plan.step: 4. Fix trap_probe's pass rule
implementation_plan.detail: Replace the flat ESCAPE_M rule. A spot escapes only if a try ends grounded within step_up of the drop-in level (the source edge's height, passed as TRAP_FROM, or the map's walkable level near the spot) or reaches a StuckScan backward-reachable node or a portal trigger. Also try 16 directions with running jumps and Up held. Keep the two Iteration Two spots. Update test_playtest_traps.gd to count probed spots from KNOWN_TRAPS.size() instead of the hard-coded 2.

implementation_plan.step: 5. Fix the corner slots in the Blender source
implementation_plan.detail:
First inspect one corner in Blender (with the MCP look tools) to confirm the root cause: the plinth top is rounded and only 0.8 m wide on portal sides (world.py:158-166), while the ring is square at +1 m and the skirt top lies about 2.25 m below.

**Preferred source fix (the brief: fix in Blender):** in plinth() make the top cover the whole ring band.
- Give every side, including thin portal sides, a margin of at least the ring offset (1.0 m) plus a little.
- Cap the corner radius so the square ring corner (+1, +1) lies inside the plinth top (radius <= margin x (2 + sqrt 2), or square corners for thin sides).
- Or add per-corner filler terraces at top - 0.2 (the P17_P25_Fill pattern from m1000000_FieldWestOfAmherst.py:411).

Keep the 4.5 m gate corridors and the 30->40 ledge invariant intact.

**Alternative if inspection shows the plinth must stay rounded:** make the ring follow the plinth top outline at corners, through region-extension style ring lines or ContainmentBuilder corner chamfers. This is runtime adaptation data, not a teleport failsafe, but it should be documented as an adaptation.

Then rebuild with scripts/build_runtime.sh, rescan, and run scripts/validate.py.

Add a Blender-side guard to scripts/validate.py, modelled on its existing trail_ring_band check: for every exterior map, sample the ring line (footprint + 1 m) inset by the body radius 0.3 m. Every sample must have the map's top cap or ground within step_up below the adjacent cap, or else a wall.
files: game/scripts/world/containment_builder.gd (only if the alternative is chosen)

New game/tools/playtest/playtest_kit.gd (class PlaytestKit, built on PlaytestDriver; the driver is already 1786 lines). Promote the duplicated scenario helpers into it, then refactor test_e/test_c/test_d to use them.

Helpers:
- travel_to(map): BFS over canonical portals with walk_trail and enter_portal; refuses a path that needs 40->30; logs a WARN and returns false instead of falling back to the console in strict mode.
- converse(goals): from test_e _converse.
- answer_quiz(qid, wrong_first := false): resolves the correct choice by TEXT from canonical quests/<id>.json dialogue.on_completion.quiz.choices[].correct, and checks wrong_answer_responses when wrong_first is set.
- use_item(id, via): double-click or quickslot.
- equip(id)
- allocate_ap(stat, n): through the stats window.
- drink_until(hp_frac)
- rest_until(hp_frac): stand still or sit, which exercises the new natural-regen rule.
- respawn(): death notice OK.
- pickup_all_nearby: gains the precise final approach from _step_onto. The canonical pickup box is 25 px each side, about 0.625 m with WorldScale.actor.
- open_shop(npc)
- checkpoint(tag): records level, EXP, mesos, equipment, important ETC and quest states into report notes and carry, for the brief's progression audit.

implementation_plan.step: 8. Add monster-aware walking and survival policy
implementation_plan.detail:
Options on PlaytestWalker.follow and walk_to (playtest_walker.gd):
- on_threat 'fight' | 'avoid' | 'ignore': when a live monster is within contact range on the path, or player_damaged fires, fight it with face_and_attack_nearest, or sidestep and replan with the monster's cell blocked.
- hp_floor: below it, drink a potion if one is held, else rest. Rest means standing still, or sitting once Phase 9 lands. Natural regen is 10 HP per 10 s and walking pauses it, so resting is a real strategy.

implementation_plan.detail:
One parameterised scenario, game/tools/playtest/scenarios/quest.gd, selected by QUEST_CHAIN env, plus scripts/playtest_quests.sh, which runs the chains in parallel with ISOLATE=q_<chain> and aggregates docs/runtime/QUEST_PLAYTHROUGH_REPORT.md.

Chains:
- 1000->1001 (Heena/Sera)
- 1002
- 1003->1004 (Nina/Sen, Townstreet door)
- 1005 (Todd, Sentinels)
- 1006
- 1007->1008
- 1009->1010 (Mai)
- 1011 (Biggs)
- 1012 (Pio, breakables)

Setup through the console is allowed but logged ('level 5', 'quest complete <prereq>', 'warp'). Everything the brief tests is play: availability (markers, menu entry, below-level refusal), acceptance, objective progress (Quest Log rows), completion, exact canonical rewards (EXP/mesos/items, and the random group for 1008), follow-up availability. Save/reload by process restart at the mid-objective of every chain.

**Cost:** chains are 2-20 min of game time each; drop-dependent collection quests (1011) are the long ones. That is about 2-3 h of game time in total, about 15-25 min of wall time sequentially (headless runs 7.5-12x faster than game time, plus about 25 s mirror and import per chain), or about 5 min in parallel.
